title: MedBackdoorGuard: Detecting and Mitigating Backdoor Attacks in Deep Learning Models for MRI-Based Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning classifiers trained on structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are increasingly proposed for early detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), yet the pipelines that produce these models depend on shared datasets, pre-trained weights, and federated updates that an adversary can poison. A backdoored diagnostic model behaves correctly on ordinary scans but collapses to an attacker-chosen label whenever a hidden trigger is present, which turns a prognostic instrument for cognitive aging into a silent source of misdiagnosis. This article proposes MedBackdoorGuard, a defense framework that detects and mitigates backdoor attacks in MRI-based AD and MCI classifiers without prior knowledge of the trigger. The framework couples spectral latent screening of training data with latent trigger isolation in activation space, then immunizes the model through trigger-sensitive neuron pruning and fine-tuning under an anatomical attention consistency constraint that anchors the decision on medial temporal structures. A runtime inference guard adds superimposition entropy and anatomically informed reconstruction to purify suspicious scans at deployment. Across ADNI, OASIS-1, and a public four-class dementia MRI benchmark under patch, blended, warping, and frequency triggers, MedBackdoorGuard reduces the mean attack success rate from 97.4% to 3.0% while holding clean accuracy within 0.6 percentage points of the undefended model, reaches a poisoned-sample detection AUROC of 97.4%, and identifies 59 of 60 backdoored models. Compared with the strongest defense baseline, attack success rate falls by 15.1 percentage points and clean accuracy rises by 1.7 percentage points. The framework restores MCI recall on triggered scans from 3.9% to 88.3%, which is the outcome that matters for early detection in cognitive aging.

title: Pelvic Floor Morphometric Differences in Women with Urinary Incontinence: A Comparative Urogynecologic Study Using Static MRI
abstract: Background: /Objectives: To compare static pelvic floor MRI morphometry between women with symptom-defined urinary incontinence (UI) and continent women and to examine whether observed differences persisted after accounting for parity and other clinical covariates. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional comparative study included 131 women: 81 classified as having symptom-defined UI and 50 continent participants. UI classification was based on self-reported involuntary urinary leakage together with at least one positive response in the urinary distress domain of the PFDI-20; no urodynamic or objective continence test was used for study classification. Static 3.0-T pelvic MRI at rest was used to measure puborectalis thickness, genital hiatus dimensions, urethral morphology, obturator internus thickness, and rectus muscle thickness. Group comparisons, exploratory within-sample ROC analyses, and parsimonious logistic regression models were performed. Results: Women with symptom-defined UI had lower bilateral puborectalis thickness (left: 5.54 ± 1.59 vs. 6.76 ± 1.33 mm; right: 5.53 ± 1.67 vs. 6.51 ± 1.46 mm; p ≤ 0.001) and larger genital hiatus width (105.54 ± 15.97 vs. 93.07 ± 15.07 mm; p < 0.001) and area (median 396.9 vs. 308.1 mm²; p < 0.001). Urethral diameter was also greater (12.34 ± 1.91 vs. 11.60 ± 1.45 mm; p = 0.021). Discrimination was moderate for genital hiatus width (AUC = 0.720) and left puborectalis thickness (AUC = 0.730). In separate parity-adjusted models, hiatus dimensions and bilateral puborectalis thickness remained associated with UI. None retained statistical significance when age, BMI, parity, and multiple correlated morphometric measures were entered together in broader models. Conclusions: Women with symptom-defined UI showed differences in puborectalis thickness and genital hiatus dimensions on static MRI. These associations were evident in unadjusted and parity-adjusted analyses but were attenuated in broader multivariable models, indicating important confounding and shared variance with clinical factors. The exploratory thresholds were derived within this sample and should not be interpreted as diagnostic cut-offs. Static MRI morphometry may help characterize pelvic floor anatomy, but the present data do not support its use as a stand-alone diagnostic test for UI.

title: Prevalence, Clinical Correlates, and Prognostic Significance of Right Ventricular Dysfunction in Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Retrospective Cohort Study from a Tertiary Referral Hospital in Somalia
abstract: Background: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) reflects the hemodynamic consequences of acute pulmonary arterial obstruction and is an important prognostic marker in patients with PE. However, data regarding the prevalence, clinical correlates, and prognostic significance of RVD remain limited in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Somalia, where diagnostic and critical care resources are constrained. Objective: To determine the prevalence and clinical correlates of RVD among adults with acute PE and to assess its association with in-hospital mortality at a tertiary referral hospital in Mogadishu, Somalia. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included adults aged ≥18 years with acute PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) who were admitted to Mogadishu Somali–Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan Training and Research Hospital between January 2020 and December 2023. RVD was defined as structural or functional right ventricular impairment documented on transthoracic echocardiography or CTPA. Demographic, clinical, comorbidity, imaging, treatment, and outcome data were extracted from medical records. Associations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests, as appropriate. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality. Results: Among 293 patients, the mean age was 59.2 years, and 201 patients (68.6%) were female. RVD was identified in 110 patients (37.5%). Compared with patients without RVD, those with RVD had higher prevalences of hypertension (46.4% vs. 34.4%; p=0.042) and pre-existing heart failure (19.1% vs. 9.8%; p=0.024). Patients with RVD were more likely to require intensive care admission (92.7% vs. 59.0%; p<0.001) and to present with hypoxemia (91.8% vs. 58.5%; p<0.001) and syncope (12.7% vs. 1.6%; p<0.001). Active malignancy was more frequent among patients with RVD, although the difference was not statistically significant (12.7% vs. 6.6%; p=0.081). Overall, 51 patients (17.4%) died during hospitalization. Mortality was significantly higher among patients with RVD than among those without RVD (29.1% vs. 10.4%; p<0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hypoxemia, and intensive care admission, RVD remained independently associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.30–5.04; p=0.007). Conclusions: RVD was present in more than one-third of Somali adults hospitalized with acute PE and was independently associated with a more than two-fold increase in the odds of in-hospital mortality. Routine assessment of right ventricular function may improve early risk stratification and support prioritization of intensive care resources in resource-limited settings.

title: Automated Detection of Coronary Artery Calcification via Machine Learning Analysis of 12-Lead Electrocardiograms
abstract: Background: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is a critical marker of subclinical atherosclerosis, yet its primary diagnostic tool, coronary computed tomography (CT), is limited by cost and radiation. We aimed to develop and validate a robust machine learning framework to identify significant CAC (Agatston score ≥100) using features extracted from routine 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), including legacy archives stored as PDFs. Methods: This retrospective study utilized 382 consecutive patient records. A novel signal-processing pipeline was developed to convert PDF-based ECGs into standardized 500-Hz digital waveforms (WFDB format). From these signals, 360 morphological and temporal features were extracted using the NeuroKit2 library. To ensure clinical reliability and prevent optimistic bias, a Balanced Random Forest (BRF) classifier was integrated into a repeated “inner-outer” nested cross-validation framework combined with Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) feature selection. Results: The mRMR-BRF model demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy with a grand mean AUC of 0.8211 (95% CI: 0.8018–0.8404), outperforming standard algorithms. Explainability analysis via SHAP identified age, ST-segment level in lead V4, T/QRS ratio in lead III, and QRS duration dispersion as the most significant predictors. These features suggest that latent electrical signatures of subclinical myocardial remodeling and impaired perfusion are detectable via AI-enhanced ECG analysis. Conclusion: Our framework establishes digitized 12-lead ECGs as a scalable and non-invasive digital biomarker for significant CAC. By enabling the quantitative analysis of legacy PDF archives and providing high predictive stability through nested validation, this approach offers a cost-effective pre-screening tool to prioritize high-risk patients for definitive imaging and early preventive intervention.

title: Pediatric Pleural Empyema: Disease Complexity, Contemporary Management, and Future Research Priorities
abstract: Background: Pediatric pleural empyema remains a major complication of community-acquired pneumonia despite vaccination and advances in minimally invasive treatment. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on etiology, diagnosis, antimicrobial therapy, pleural drainage, fibrinolysis, and surgery. Methods: PubMed was searched from inception through July 2026 for English-language studies involving patients aged 0–18 years. Pediatric trials, observational studies, surveillance reports, guidelines, reviews, and relevant case series were considered. Of 42 publications assessed in full, 38 were included in the narrative synthesis. Results: Streptococcus pneumoniae, particularly serotype 3, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pyogenes remain the principal pathogens. Chest ultrasound is preferred for characterizing pleural collections and guiding intervention, whereas computed tomography is reserved for atypical disease or suspected complications. Small, uncomplicated effusions may respond to antibiotics alone; large, purulent, or clinically significant collections generally require source control. Image-guided small-bore catheter drainage with protocol-based urokinase or tissue plasminogen activator is effective for many loculated effusions. Pediatric evidence does not support routine addition of DNase. Comparative trials show broadly similar clinical outcomes for fibrinolysis and video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, although heterogeneous protocols and limited sample sizes preclude identification of a universally superior strategy. Thoracotomy is rarely required. Conclusions: Management should integrate respiratory and septic severity, pleural anatomy, microbiology, adequacy of drainage, clinical trajectory, and local expertise rather than rely on rigid staging. Long-term recovery is excellent in most previously healthy children receiving timely treatment. Standardized definitions, pediatric outcome sets, multicenter comparative trials, validated predictors of treatment failure, and studies of antimicrobial duration remain important research priorities.

title: Salivary Polyamines Are Effective Biomarkers for Gastric Cancer Detection
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Gastric cancer (GC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, highlighting the need for minimally invasive and highly accurate screening methods for its early detection. We evaluated the utility of salivary polyamine-based metabolomic analysis for distinguishing individuals with GC from those without GC. Methods: A total of 53 patients with GC and 37 non-GC controls were included. Participants were recruited from individuals who underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy at Tokyo Medical University Hospital between March 2020 and May 2025 and provided saliva samples on the same day. Participants with factors known to affect polyamine levels were excluded. Salivary metabolites quantified by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry were statistically compared between groups. Acetylated-to-non-acetylated polyamine ratios were used as features to construct a logistic regression-based machine learning model, and discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results: The GC group showed significantly higher concentrations of salivary metabolites. Among individual polyamines, N1-acetylspermine demonstrated the highest discriminative ability (AUC = 0.845). When acetylated-to-non-acetylated polyamine ratios were analyzed, significant differences between groups were observed for N1,N8-diacetylspermidine/spermidine and N1-acetylspermine/spermine. A logistic regression model constructed using six such ratios achieved strong predictive performance in the test dataset (AUC = 0.807), with a sensitivity of 81.3% and a specificity of 72.7%. Notably, these ratios outperformed conventional tumor markers such as carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen 19-9, in sensitivity. Conclusions: Our results demonstrate that salivary polyamine analysis, particularly using acetylation ratios, enables accurate and minimally invasive detection of GC and represents a promising adjunctive tool for GC screening.

title: A Case Report of Late Infantile Krabbe Disease: Expanding the Genotype-Phenotype Correlation and Autopsy Findings
abstract: Krabbe disease (KD) is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative lysosomal disease typically caused by pathogenic variants in GALC, which encodes for the lysosomal galactosylceramidase enzyme. Age of onset is variable, with earlier symptom onset conferring a more severe, and ultimately fatal, disease course. We present a case of an 18-month-old previously healthy female diagnosed with late-infantile KD following a 3-month period of psychomotor regression and irritability. Clinical features included severe axial hypotonia with lower extremity spasticity and hyperreflexia. Whole genome sequencing disclosed a complex GALC genotype including two likely pathogenic variants, p.(Gly284Ser) and p.(Tyr314del), which had not been observed in compound heterozygosity prior. Magnetic resonance imaging displayed symmetric T2 hyperintensity of the central-parietal white matter. The patient ultimately died 6 months after diagnosis from rapidly progressing neurological deterioration. There was significant atrophy on neuropathologic examination, with diffuse globoid cell infiltrate at the supratentorial and infratentorial white matter with relative sparing of the frontal lobe on light microscopy. This patient’s novel genotype, imaging and pathologic findings expand our understanding of the phenotype-genotype correlation in individuals with KD.

title: XAI-AttnFusionNet+: Explainable Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Early Screening of Pediatric Language Impairment Using rs-fMRI with Hierarchical Attention Fusion
abstract: Pediatric Language Impairment requires timely and consistent screening to enable early intervention and to improve long-term developmental outcomes. Nevertheless, current methods struggle to extract clinically relevant biomarkers from high-dimensional and heterogeneous neuroimaging data, particularly when multimodal analyses and interpretable modeling are not involved. To address these limitations, this paper presents XAI-AttnFusionNet+, an explainable multimodal deep learning model for early-stage Language Impairment screening with early childhood resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI). The proposed model integrates spatial patterns of brain activation, dynamic functional connectivity, and clinical phenotypic characteristics through a hierarchical attention-based fusion mechanism enabling adaptive modality weighting and improved representation learning. To enhance transparency and clinical interpretability, post hoc explainability methods, such as attention visualization, Grad-CAM, and SHAP, were employed to identify discriminative brain regions and feature contributions. The framework was evaluated on a multicenter pediatric cohort of 255 subjects based on ABIDE II using a Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) validation protocol and further evaluated for cross-dataset generalization using ABIDE I. In the absence of Language Impairment annotations, proxy labels were constructed based on phenotypic language indicators. The performance of XAI-AttnFusionNet+ with an accuracy of 93.3% and an AUC of 0.968 outperforms the traditional unimodal baseline models and demonstrates strong cross-site generalization. The results indicate the potential of the proposed framework as a neuroimaging-based approach for early detection of Language Impairment risk. However, its deployment in real-world settings requires further validation using clinically annotated datasets.

title: Successful Nonsurgical Management of Norovirus-Triggered Necrotizing Enterocolitis in a Preterm Infant: What Is the Role of Immunomodulation?
abstract: Norovirus infection has been increasingly recognized as a potential trigger of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm neonates. Although previous reports have described severe cases associated with intestinal pneumatosis, bowel ischemia, and the need for surgical intervention, the clinical spectrum of Norovirus-related intestinal disease remains poorly defined. We report the case of a 29-week gestational age preterm infant who developed abdominal distension on the 35th day of life. Stool reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction confirmed Norovirus infection. Abdominal radiographs showed progressive development of intestinal pneumatosis, leading to the confirmed diagnosis of a stage IIA NEC. Abdominal pneumatosis resolved completely within five days, without evidence of perforation or clinical deterioration. The infant received only supportive therapy and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). This case highlighted the heterogeneous clinical spectrum of Norovirus-associated intestinal involvement in preterm infants and the possible protective and immunomodulatory role of the IVIG.

title: AT(N)-Anchored Multimodal Deep Learning for Alzheimer’s Staging: A Taxonomy and Continuous Burden Index for Low-Resource Settings
abstract: The global burden of dementia is heavily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet biological diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) relies on positron emission tomography (PET) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis that are operationally inaccessible in these regions. The 2024 Alzheimer’s Association revised criteria recognize sufficiently accurate plasma assays,particularly p-tau217,as Core 1 biomarkers that may support biological diagnosis, offering a scientifically credible pathway to infrastructure-light biological detection and staging. However, the machine learning literature has expanded without principled mapping to the AT(N) biological framework or rigorous consideration of deployability constraints in resource limited settings. We present a systematic scoping review synthesizing 146 included full-text publications (2018–2026) across four multidisciplinary evidence streams, establishing a novel architectural taxonomy that maps deep learning architectural families directly to AT(N) biological targets and connects model inductive biases to specific biomarker categories. We audit major AD datasets, identify critical biases in demographic and biomarker representation, and map pervasive data pathologies—label scarcity, missing modalities, scanner heterogeneity, and population bias—to corresponding ML/DL remediation strategies. Finally, we argue for a shift from binary classification toward continuous, biologically anchored disease-burden scoring, proposing the Alzheimer’s Disease Burden Index (ADBI). The ADBI equations presented herein represent a theoretical and architectural framework designed to guide future prospective validation on multi-ethnic cohorts. This work provides a methodological roadmap for developing globally deployable, equity aware AD diagnostic models.

title: Osteosarcopenia Predicts Mortality in Metastatic Prostate Cancer: A Longitudinal Analysis of Opportunistic CT Imaging
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Osteoporosis and sarcopenia are associated with fractures, falls, and mortality. In prostate cancer, aging, advanced disease, and androgen deprivation therapy may accelerate concurrent bone and muscle loss. This study characterized longitudinal CT-derived musculoskeletal biomarkers in metastatic prostate cancer and evaluated the association between baseline osteosarcopenia and overall survival. Methods: This retrospective single-centre cohort included patients treated from 2009 to 2022, with follow-up imaging through 2024. An automated deep-learning pipeline quantified lumbar trabecular bone mineral density (BMD), psoas muscle volume (PV), psoas muscle density (PD), and volumetric psoas muscle index (vPMI). Osteosarcopenia was defined as concurrent osteoporosis (BMD < 135 HU) and sarcopenia (vPMI < 30). Survival from baseline CT was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Results: Among 437 patients with 3389 CT scans, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, and osteosarcopenia increased from 29.6%, 46.9%, and 17.2% at baseline to 54.0%, 82.8%, and 45.5% at final imaging. BMD declined by 2.1-3.7% annually, PD by 3.2-3.9%, and PV by 3.6-4.6% (all p < 0.0001). In the final year of life, PD declined by 12.0% and PV by 9.3%. Baseline osteosarcopenia remained independently associated with mortality after adjustment for age, time from diagnosis to baseline CT, PSA, and Gleason risk group (HR 2.11, 95% CI 1.50-2.99; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Osteosarcopenia is common and progressive in metastatic prostate cancer, and muscle loss accelerates near death. Baseline osteosarcopenia independently identifies patients at increased mortality risk. Automated analysis of routine surveillance CT may enable longitudinal musculoskeletal assessment and prognostic risk stratification.

title: Distilling Multimodal Biomedical Foundation Models for Edge Tuberculosis Screening: Client-Side WebAssembly Deployment and Conformal Clinical Abstention
abstract: Background: Deep learning for tuberculosis triage risks shortcut learning and overconfidence. We evaluate distilling BioMedCLIP into an edge-deployable architecture with a selective conformal safety interlock. Methods: A DenseNet-121 student (7.74M parameters) was trained on 12,599 radiographs via Tri-Loss distillation from a frozen BioMedCLIP teacher (86.4M parameters). Validation evaluated 3,441 radiographs: a primary within-scanner clinical benchmark (Combined India: Solan N=155, NITRD N=278) and an adversarial compression stress-test (Pakistan N=3,008). Mondrian split-conformal prediction calibrated a three-tiered interlock: urgent molecular testing, autonomous clearance, and clinical referral. Findings: Distillation significantly outperformed the supervised baseline: Solan AUROC 0.9449 vs 0.8613; NITRD AUROC 0.9520 vs 0.8718; Combined India AUROC 0.9497 vs 0.8635; and Pakistan AUROC 0.8624 vs 0.4990 (all p < 0.0001). In Indian hospital cohorts, the system referred 63.1% of ambiguous active TB cases to clinicians, flagging 32.5% as urgent for GeneXpert testing, while autonomously clearing 77.4% of healthy controls (178/230). Against total screening volume (3,441 external scans), the interlock achieved an unconditional false-clearance rate of 0.26% (9/3,441; 0.00% on cavitary MDR-TB development proxy). Among confirmed active TB cases, the false-negative discharge rate was 4.4% in India (9/203, down from 16.3% on baseline) and 0.0% in Pakistan (0/2,494), counterbalanced by 63.1% clinical referral. Pure graph execution latency of the 27.0 MB WebAssembly model was 77.5 ms on reference x86_64 CPU. Interpretation: Distilling foundation models into selective classification networks reconciles diagnostic accuracy with edge efficiency. Rather than forcing uncalibrated decisions, the system clears normal scans, expedites molecular assays for high-confidence TB, and safely refers diagnostic ambiguity to clinicians. Funding: Independent departmental resources; no external commercial funding.

title: AI-Driven Retinal Screening: A Stacked Machine Learning Framework for Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Detection in Routine Medical Checkups Using a Public Fundus Database
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness, yet large numbers of people with diabetes miss their annual eye examination because grading retinal photographs requires scarce specialists. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) based eye-inspection framework that embeds automated DR screening inside a routine general medical checkup. The framework comprises five layers: image acquisition, automated quality control, lesion feature extraction, a stacked machine learning (ML) decision engine, and an explainable clinical report with referral. We evaluate the approach on the public UCI Diabetic Retinopathy Debrecen database, which contains 19 lesion, anatomical and image-level features extracted from 1,151 MESSIDOR fundus images. Nine classical and neural classifiers are benchmarked with 10-fold stratified cross-validation, after which the proposed pipeline adds lesion-aware feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning and stacked generalization. The proposed model reaches a cross-validated area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.854 and accuracy of 77.6%, improving the logistic-regression baseline by 0.029 AUC, and achieves a hold-out AUC of 0.878 (95% bootstrap CI 0.830–0.917) with 79.7% sensitivity and 77.6% specificity. Lowering the decision threshold to 0.30 yields 91.9% sensitivity for screening use. In an extension to cataract, three image-clarity features separate normal from cataract fundus images with a cross-validated AUC of 0.978. Permutation importance and ablation show that microaneurysm counts carry most of the diagnostic signal, consistent with clinical grading. Using CDC surveillance data covering 9.6 million Americans with DR, we project that the screening operating point would detect 8.8 million cases while removing about 16 million specialist grading visits per year. We discuss clinical workflow integration, challenges including domain shift, bias and regulation, and a roadmap towards deep-learning-based multi-disease retinal screening.

title: Detector-Stage Failures in Box-Prompted Glioma Segmentation: A Three-Arm Analysis Across Two External Cohorts
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Whether the detector or the segmenter fails externally is unknown in a box-prompted pipeline; an oracle-box arm separates them by prompting with the ground-truth box. Methods: A real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR) with Segment Anything Model (SAM) 2.1 was evaluated against MedSAM3 with a low-rank adaptation (LoRA) adapter on 158 glioma cases from three cohorts. Three arms decompose the gap into a detector-stage term and a residual; a fourth splits the residual. Results: At whole tumour the cost of finding the box rises from +0.006 Dice in domain to +0.091 on the Brain Tumour Segmentation (BraTS) Africa cohort, a difference of +0.085 [+0.045, +0.130] that survives a second detector seed and a second segmenter. The Río Hortega University Hospital glioblastoma cohort (RHUH-GBM) did not show a statistically resolved increase; the two external cohorts differ by +0.073 [+0.035, +0.116]. On BraTS-Africa, slices with no box carry the term, not poorly placed boxes. The in-domain baseline is not categorical: the term excludes zero under a matched prompt and on tumour core. Nine of 95 pipeline cases fall below 0.5 Dice; a post hoc coverage flag identifies seven. Conclusions: On BraTS-Africa, but not RHUH-GBM, the increase in pipeline deficit was primarily associated with the detector stage.

title: Biocompatibility and Osseointegration of Plasma-Anodized Additively Manufactured Co–Cr–Mo Implants in a Rat Critical-Size Calvarial Defect Model
abstract: Background: Additive manufacturing has emerged as a promising technology for the fabrication of patient-specific metallic implants with complex architectures for craniofacial reconstruction. Among metallic biomaterials, cobalt–chromium–molybdenum (Co–28Cr–6Mo) alloys exhibit excellent mechanical strength and corrosion resistance. Plasma anodization has been proposed as a surface engineering strategy to enhance the biological performance of metallic implants; how-ever, its ability to improve osseointegration and bone regeneration remains uncertain. This study investigated the biological response of plasma-anodized additively manufactured Co–28Cr–6Mo implants in a rat critical-size calvarial defect model. Methods: Forty-eight male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to eight experimental groups (n = 6 per group) receiving untreated Co–28Cr–6Mo implants, plasma-anodized Co–28Cr–6Mo implants, titanium-coated plas-ma-anodized Co–28Cr–6Mo implants, or empty defects (control). Animals were euthanized after 6 or 12 weeks. Biological performance was assessed by macroscopic and radiographic examina-tions, histological analyses (Stevens Blue and Von Kossa staining), and quantitative histomor-phometric evaluation of newly formed bone area. Results: All implant surfaces demonstrated excellent in vivo biocompatibility, with no evidence of chronic inflammation, implant rejection, corrosion, or postoperative complications throughout the experimental period. Histological analyses consistently revealed limited bone formation confined to the margins of the defects and the persistence of fibrous connective tissue between the implant surface and the host bone. Quan-titative histomorphometry showed a slight increase in newly formed bone after 12 weeks com-pared with 6 weeks; however, no statistically significant differences were observed among the Control, Co–28Cr–6Mo, Co–28Cr–6Mo PIII, and Co–28Cr–6Mo/Ti PIII groups (p > 0.05). Conclu-sions: Plasma anodization preserved the excellent biocompatibility of additively manufactured Co–28Cr–6Mo implants but did not significantly improve osseointegration or bone regeneration in a rat critical-size calvarial defect model. These findings indicate that plasma anodization alone is insufficient to enhance the regenerative performance of Co–Cr–Mo implants and suggest that additional bioactive surface functionalization strategies may be necessary to promote bone re-pair in critical-size craniofacial defects.

title: Detection and Decision-Making for Secondary Caries: A Scoping Review Informing a Clinical Decision Framework
abstract: Background: Secondary caries or caries around restorations or sealants is a common reason for replacement of restorations. However, distinguishing true secondary caries from restoration-related defects remains clinically difficult and may lead to overtreatment and unnecessary removal of healthy tooth structure. Objectives: This scoping review aimed to map how diagnostic strategies for secondary caries are used and how these findings are translated into treatment decisions, while identifying diagnostic thresholds and informing an evidence-based decision framework. Methods: Searches were performed in seven electronic databases, gray literature sources, and guideline repositories without restrictions on language or publication year. Evidence addressing diagnostic strategies for secondary caries, as well as relevant guidelines and consensus documents, were included. Data were organized descriptively, and the methodological quality of primary studies was critically evaluated. Results: Forty-eight documents were included (34 original studies and 14 guidelines or consensus statements). Visual–tactile examination, commonly combined with bitewings, was the most frequently reported detection approach. Adjunctive methods, including fluorescence-based devices, optical imaging, and artificial intelligence, were investigated as complementary detection tools, with heterogeneous performance across study designs. Treatment decisions were primarily driven by lesion activity and suspected dentine involvement rather than marginal appearance alone. Explicit diagnostic thresholds were rarely predefined, and substantial variability was observed in how diagnostic findings informed treatment decisions. Conclusions: The evidence supports visual–tactile assessment complemented by bitewings as first-line approaches within a diagnostic strategy for secondary caries evaluation. However, heterogeneity in diagnostic thresholds and treatment decision criteria limits comparability across studies and may contribute to inconsistent clinical management. Greater standardization in reporting diagnostic strategies and decision frameworks is needed to support evidence-based and conservative care. Clinical significance: This review provides an evidence-informed clinical framework based on visual–tactile and radiographic assessment for secondary caries around restorations. By integrating detection methods, lesion interpretation, and commonly reported clinical thresholds, the framework illustrates how findings from routine assessment are translated into treatment strategies. The findings indicate that treatment decisions are more consistently guided by lesion activity and dentine involvement than by restoration defects alone, supporting a more conservative approach under diagnostic uncertainty and highlighting the need for greater standardization in clinical criteria.

title: MC-Former: Motion Correction in Brain MRI Using Vision Transformers and Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Background: Motion during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is common and can degrade image quality and reduce diagnostic accuracy. This study developed MC-Former, a motion correction method for brain MRI based on vision transformers and self-supervised learning. Methods: Motion-free brain MRI data from 52 subjects were used to generate 13,700 training, 1,950 validation, and 4,680 test axial slices from 3D sagittal T1-weighted scans acquired at 3T. MC-Former was derived from a vision transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture with skip connections. During self-supervised pre-training, 50% of patches from motion-free images were randomly masked and reconstructed; synthetic motion-corrupted images were then used for supervised training. Evaluation was performed on simulated motion-corrupted axial images unseen during training, using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Results: MC-Former improved PSNR from 26.4 to 32.8 and SSIM from 0.77 to 0.94, significantly outperforming MC-Net and Restormer on the test set. For motion-free images, MC-Former achieved SSIM > 0.99. Conclusion: These results indicate that MC-Former effectively suppresses simulated motion artifacts in brain MRI while preserving artifact-free image quality. The code and trained model are available at https://github.com/MRIMoCo/MC-Former.

Background:

Motion during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is common and can degrade image quality and reduce diagnostic accuracy. This study developed MC-Former, a motion correction method for brain MRI based on vision transformers and self-supervised learning.

Methods:

Motion-free brain MRI data from 52 subjects were used to generate 13,700 training, 1,950 validation, and 4,680 test axial slices from 3D sagittal T1-weighted scans acquired at 3T. MC-Former was derived from a vision transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture with skip connections. During self-supervised pre-training, 50% of patches from motion-free images were randomly masked and reconstructed; synthetic motion-corrupted images were then used for supervised training. Evaluation was performed on simulated motion-corrupted axial images unseen during training, using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM).

Results:

MC-Former improved PSNR from 26.4 to 32.8 and SSIM from 0.77 to 0.94, significantly outperforming MC-Net and Restormer on the test set. For motion-free images, MC-Former achieved SSIM > 0.99.

Conclusion:

These results indicate that MC-Former effectively suppresses simulated motion artifacts in brain MRI while preserving artifact-free image quality. The code and trained model are available at https://github.com/MRIMoCo/MC-Former.

title: Platelet-Derived Extracellular Vesicles for the Diagnosis of Ovarian Cancer
abstract: Objective: Differentiating ovarian cancer from benign and borderline adnexal lesions remains challenging. We previously identified nine platelet protein markers associated with ovarian cancer. This study aimed to validate these markers on platelet-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) and assess their ability to distinguish ovarian cancer from benign and borderline adnexal lesions. Methods: Patients were recruited between 2021 and 2025 at Uppsala University Hospital and Gävle Hospital, Sweden, and grouped according to postoperative histopathological diagnosis. Platelet-free plasma samples were analyzed by flow cytometry. Platelet-derived EVs (CD41+) and nine platelet protein markers (ACTN4, CRKL, ERP29, GELS, MAP1A, MYCT1, PHB, RELN, and SRC) were quantified on CD41+CD62P+ and CD41+CD62P− EV populations. Group differences were assessed using non-parametric tests, binary and proportional odds logistic regression, and Boruta feature selection. Results: Total CD41+ EVs and CD41+CD62P+ EVs did not differ between groups. Levels of CD62P+anti-GELS, CD62P+anti-SRC, and CD62P−anti-MYCT1 were highest in ovarian cancer. CD62P+anti-GELS was independently associated with ovarian cancer in both crude analysis (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.16-1.85; C-statistic 0.63) and analysis adjusted for age and CA125 (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.21-2.08; C-statistic 0.82). Boruta algorithm identified ultrasound assessment and CA125, followed by CD62P+anti-GELS, CD62P−anti-SRC, CD62P−anti-ERP29, CD62P−anti-MAP1A, and CD62P+anti-ACTN4, as the variables associated with ovarian cancer. CD62P+anti-ERP29 was specifically associated with advanced-stage ovarian cancer compared with other abdominal malignancies (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.53-4.38; C-statistic 0.85). Conclusion: CD62P+anti-GELS on platelet EVs was independently associated with ovarian cancer after adjustment for age and CA125. Together with CD62P+/CD62P− anti-SRC, CD62P+anti-ACTN4, CD62P−anti-ERP29 and CD62P−anti-MAP1A, it may complement ultrasound evaluation and CA125 in distinguishing ovarian cancer from benign and borderline adnexal lesions.

title: Complete Spontaneous Remodeling of a Severely Angulated Traumatic Fetal Femoral Shaft Fracture: Prenatal Healing, Neonatal Malunion, and 12-Year Follow-up
abstract: Background: Fetal long-bone fractures are rare and may result from maternal trauma, skeletal dysplasia, or, less commonly, apparently spontaneous events. Prenatal diagnosis is primarily based on ultrasonography, while the subsequent course of fetal fracture healing and long-term remodeling remains poorly documented. Case Presentation: A 35-week fetus sustained a displaced mid-diaphyseal fracture of the right femur following a maternal frontal motor vehicle collision. Initial ultrasonography demonstrated approximately 68° of interfragmentary angulation and surrounding soft-tissue edema. Maternal and fetal surveillance over the following 7 days showed no evidence of fetal compromise. Serial ultrasound examinations demonstrated progressive callus formation, with a globular membranous callus at day 7 and a prominent hyperechoic callus with peripheral vascularization and reduced fragment mobility at day 14. Delivery occurred by cesarean section at 39+2 weeks for an obstetric indication. The newborn weighed 3150 g and had Apgar scores of 9 and 10. The fracture was clinically consolidated but remained in severe malunion, with approximately 56° of ventrolateral angulation and a clinically estimated 6.5 cm apparent clinical shortening. No orthopedic intervention was undertaken. Progressive spontaneous correction was documented, with residual angulation of 35° at 3 months and 15° at 6 months. By 10 months, complete angular correction and limb-length equalization were documented. Independent walking was achieved at 12 months. At 12 years of age, the child had normal limb alignment, equal limb lengths, normal gait, and no functional sequelae. Conclusions: This case demonstrates an unusual combination of prenatal fracture healing, severe neonatal malunion, and complete long-term spontaneous correction without orthopedic intervention. The reported 6.5-cm shortening should be interpreted as apparent clinical shortening rather than definitive anatomical shortening because it was not established by standardized radiographic limb-length measurement. Geometric analysis indicates that angular deformity alone could account for only approximately 0.8–1.0 cm of shortening at term. The subsequent course is consistent with substantial growth-related remodeling and provides a rare longitudinal example of the remodeling potential of the immature femur.

title: Spinal cord stimulation for cancer pain: a narrative review of mechanistic rationale, clinical integration, and emerging applications.
abstract: Background and objective Pain remains one of the most prevalent symptoms among patients with advanced cancer, with a substantial subset experiencing persistent pain despite optimized pharmacologic management. Although spinal cord stimulation (SCS) has emerged as a potential neuromodulatory option for refractory cancer-related pain, its role within contemporary multidisciplinary cancer pain management remains incompletely defined. This narrative review examines the mechanistic rationale, clinical applications, guideline positioning, and practical implementation of SCS across cancer pain phenotypes. Methods A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and relevant guideline sources from database inception through May 21, 2026. Search terms included combinations of "spinal cord stimulation", "SCS", "neuromodulation", "cancer pain", "cancer-related pain", "refractory cancer pain", "palliative care", "chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy", "CIPN", "intrathecal drug delivery", "dorsal root ganglion stimulation", and "peripheral nerve stimulation". English-language clinical studies (prospective and retrospective), case reports, case series, systematic, scoping, and narrative reviews, guideline statements, and relevant preclinical studies were considered. Key content and findings Available evidence, consisting predominantly of retrospective cohorts and case-based literature without randomized trials, suggests that SCS may provide clinically meaningful pain relief and opioid-sparing benefit in selected patients with refractory cancer pain. This review contextualizes SCS within contemporary cancer pain management by examining its mechanistic foundations, waveform evolution, patient selection, prognosis-sensitive decision-making, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) compatibility, and comparative positioning relative to intrathecal drug delivery systems and other interventional therapies. Emerging applications, particularly in chemotherapy-induced neuropathy and survivorship-related pain syndromes, are also discussed. Conclusions SCS represents a promising yet selectively applicable modality for refractory cancer-related pain, particularly among patients with neuropathic and mixed pain phenotypes inadequately controlled with pharmacotherapy alone. Rather than functioning as a competing alternative to existing cancer pain interventions, SCS should be considered within a broader, multidisciplinary, phenotype-informed framework that includes guideline-directed pharmacologic care, interventional procedures, and neuromodulatory strategies such as intrathecal drug delivery. Future prospective studies are needed not only to clarify efficacy but also to refine patient selection and optimize the integration of SCS into modern cancer pain care.

title: Time-zero multimodal risk stratification for in-hospital mortality in acute aortic dissection: two-centre development, temporal and external validation, and occult shock phenotyping.
abstract: Background Acute aortic dissection (AAD) requires rapid anatomical diagnosis and early risk stratification, yet initial blood pressure alone may miss patients with concealed hypoperfusion. Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients. Methods This retrospective two-centre cohort study included 2,584 adults with first-time AAD who completed CTA and TTE during the initial 2-hour assessment after emergency department triage. Cohorts were development (n=1,678; 2007-2017), internal temporal validation (n=452; 2018-2021), and external geographic/later-era validation (n=454; 2022-March 2024). Candidate variables were restricted to information available during this initial assessment window. Four supervised algorithms were compared, with ablation analyses assessing modality-specific contribution. Results XGBoost achieved optimism-corrected development area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.88], internal validation 0.83 (0.79-0.87), and external validation 0.78 (0.74-0.82). Adding TTE to Clinical + CTA improved discrimination (Delta AUC +0.04, P=0.002) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) (+0.021, P=0.01). Normotensive occult shock occurred in 548/2,082 patients (26.3%) and was associated with mortality 15.9% versus 6.7% in metabolically stable normotension. Conclusions In high-volume aortic centres where CTA and early TTE are routinely available, this initial 2-hour multimodal model showed temporal validation and moderate external discrimination for in-hospital mortality. TTE added prognostic information, particularly for type A disease, and normotensive hyperlactatemia identified a higher-risk subgroup; however, general use, type B performance, local recalibration, and action thresholds require prospective multicentre validation before clinical implementation.

title: Breast implant-associated late hematoma: a narrative review of case reports and case series.
abstract: Background and objective Late hematoma after breast implantation presents with delayed breast swelling or periprosthetic fluid that is clinically indistinguishable from breast implant-associated anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL), late seroma, infection, or tumor recurrence. This narrative review synthesized published case reports and small case series to describe clinical presentations, hypothesized mechanisms, diagnostic approaches, and management strategies. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to December 31, 2025. English-language case reports and case series documenting hematoma occurring ≥4 months after implantation were included. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Given the heterogeneity of uncontrolled case-level evidence, a qualitative descriptive synthesis was performed. Key content and findings There were 37 articles involving 47 cases from 12 countries included. The median time from implantation to hematoma onset was 72.0 months. Patients typically presented with acute painful unilateral swelling. Features distinguishing late hematoma from BIA-ALCL included acute pain, absence of persistent effusion beyond 1 year, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signal characteristics consistent with evolving blood products. Proposed mechanisms included capsular microfractures, chronic inflammation with neovascularization, external trauma, and iatrogenic factors such as anticoagulation. Ultrasound was the preferred initial screening tool; MRI provided definitive assessment of hematoma staging and implant integrity. Image-guided aspiration was essential to obtain fluid for cytology, microbiology, and CD30 immunohistochemistry to exclude BIA-ALCL. Surgical evacuation with capsulectomy was the most frequently reported definitive treatment; ultrasound-guided aspiration or arterial embolization were described in select patients with intact implants or poor surgical tolerance. Follow-up and recurrence data were inconsistently reported. Conclusions Late hematoma should be considered in implant recipients with delayed swelling or periprosthetic fluid. Clinical evaluation, ultrasound, MRI, and image-guided aspiration guide management. Surgical evacuation with capsulectomy remains the primary reported treatment. These findings are descriptive only.

title: Habitat-based ultrasound radiomics for preoperative prediction of axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer: a two-center study.
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative prediction of axillary lymph node metastasis (ALNM) remains challenging. This study investigates whether habitat-based ultrasound radiomics of suspicious axillary lymph nodes can predict preoperative ALNM in patients with breast cancer. Methods This retrospective two-center study included 416 breast cancer patients with suspicious axillary lymph nodes and pathologically confirmed nodal status. Patients from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University were randomly assigned to the training and internal validation cohorts at a ratio of 7:3, whereas patients from Taihe County People's Hospital constituted the external test cohort. Suspicious lymph nodes were manually segmented. Pixel-level features were clustered using the K-means algorithm to divide each node into four habitat subregions. Radiomics features were extracted from the intranodal region of interest and each habitat subregion to construct the intranodal radiomics, individual habitat, and habitat radiomics models. A combined nomogram integrating the optimal radiomics signature with independent clinical predictors was developed. Results Cortical thickness and lymph node vascular pattern were independent predictors of ALNM. The habitat radiomics model outperformed the intranodal radiomics and individual habitat models, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.859, 0.809, and 0.791 in the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, respectively. The combined nomogram achieved the highest AUCs of 0.866, 0.819, and 0.806 in the corresponding cohorts, and its clinical utility was confirmed by decision curve analysis. Conclusions Habitat-based ultrasound radiomics improved ALNM prediction by capturing intranodal heterogeneity. The nomogram may provide a practical noninvasive tool for individualized preoperative assessment of suspicious axillary lymph nodes.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound in detecting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is a key prognostic indicator in breast cancer. Whether ultrasound can reliably distinguish pCR from residual disease, and whether advanced functional ultrasound techniques add sufficient diagnostic value over conventional B-mode imaging to influence treatment decisions, remains uncertain. Given the heterogeneity in existing evidence and the lack of consensus on optimal ultrasound modalities and assessment timing, a comprehensive synthesis is needed to guide clinical practice. This study aimed to determine the overall diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound for predicting pCR after NAC in breast cancer, compare different ultrasound modalities, and identify factors influencing predictive value. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA-DTA guidelines. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from inception to April 1, 2025. Studies evaluating any ultrasound-based modality [conventional B-mode, shear-wave elastography (SWE), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), superb microvascular imaging (SMI), or quantitative ultrasound (QUS)] against histopathological reference standard (pCR defined as ypT0/is ypN0 or equivalent) were included. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Data were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model. Results Twelve studies (2,146 patients) were included. The overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.80 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.73-0.86] and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.70-0.83), respectively, with a diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) of 13.7 (95% CI: 8.2-22.9), positive likelihood ratio (PLR) of 3.5 (95% CI: 2.6-4.7), negative likelihood ratio (NLR) of 0.26 (95% CI: 0.19-0.36), and area under the curve (AUC) of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.82-0.88). Heterogeneity was substantial (τ 2 =0.58 for sensitivity, 0.43 for specificity). Advanced functional ultrasound techniques demonstrated significantly higher diagnostic accuracy (DOR =16.04, 95% CI: 12.46-20.64) compared to conventional B-mode ultrasound alone (DOR =5.26, 95% CI: 3.47-7.99; interaction P=0.003). Early assessment during NAC (after 1-2 cycles) yielded the highest predictive value (DOR =17.10, AUC =0.90). Risk of bias was generally low, though some concerns were noted in patient selection (2 retrospective studies) and flow and timing domains. Conclusions Ultrasound demonstrates moderate diagnostic accuracy for predicting pCR after NAC, with substantial heterogeneity across techniques. Advanced functional ultrasound techniques, particularly when employed early during treatment, offer superior performance. However, given the moderate sensitivity and specificity, ultrasound should be considered an adjunctive tool rather than a standalone method for pCR determination. These findings support the potential role of ultrasound in guiding adaptive therapy, but further validation with standardized protocols is needed before routine clinical implementation.

This study aimed to determine the overall diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound for predicting pCR after NAC in breast cancer, compare different ultrasound modalities, and identify factors influencing predictive value.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA-DTA guidelines. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from inception to April 1, 2025. Studies evaluating any ultrasound-based modality [conventional B-mode, shear-wave elastography (SWE), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), superb microvascular imaging (SMI), or quantitative ultrasound (QUS)] against histopathological reference standard (pCR defined as ypT0/is ypN0 or equivalent) were included. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Data were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model.

Results

Twelve studies (2,146 patients) were included. The overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.80 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.73-0.86] and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.70-0.83), respectively, with a diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) of 13.7 (95% CI: 8.2-22.9), positive likelihood ratio (PLR) of 3.5 (95% CI: 2.6-4.7), negative likelihood ratio (NLR) of 0.26 (95% CI: 0.19-0.36), and area under the curve (AUC) of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.82-0.88). Heterogeneity was substantial (τ2=0.58 for sensitivity, 0.43 for specificity). Advanced functional ultrasound techniques demonstrated significantly higher diagnostic accuracy (DOR =16.04, 95% CI: 12.46-20.64) compared to conventional B-mode ultrasound alone (DOR =5.26, 95% CI: 3.47-7.99; interaction P=0.003). Early assessment during NAC (after 1-2 cycles) yielded the highest predictive value (DOR =17.10, AUC =0.90). Risk of bias was generally low, though some concerns were noted in patient selection (2 retrospective studies) and flow and timing domains.

Conclusions

Ultrasound demonstrates moderate diagnostic accuracy for predicting pCR after NAC, with substantial heterogeneity across techniques. Advanced functional ultrasound techniques, particularly when employed early during treatment, offer superior performance. However, given the moderate sensitivity and specificity, ultrasound should be considered an adjunctive tool rather than a standalone method for pCR determination. These findings support the potential role of ultrasound in guiding adaptive therapy, but further validation with standardized protocols is needed before routine clinical implementation.

title: Habitat radiomics combined with clinical features for predicting tertiary lymphoid structure status in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: development and validation of a preoperative CECT-based model.
abstract: Background Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) are emerging prognostic biomarkers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet no reliable non-invasive tool exists for their preoperative assessment. This study aimed to develop and validate a contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT)-based habitat radiomics model for preoperative prediction of intratumoral TLS status in PDAC. Methods In this retrospective study, 204 surgically resected PDAC patients were enrolled and allocated into training (n=142) and validation (n=62) cohorts. TLS status was determined by fluorescent multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC), with positive cases subclassified as primary or secondary follicle-like TLS. K-means clustering partitioned the tumor volume of interest (VOI) into spatially distinct subregions; radiomics features were extracted from each subregion and selected via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Five machine learning classifiers were evaluated. Independent clinical predictors were identified by multivariate logistic regression (LR) and integrated with the optimal imaging model to construct a combined model. Results TLS positivity was observed in 32.84% of patients. The LR-based habitat model achieved area under the curve (AUC) of 0.939 and 0.873 in the training and validation cohorts, substantially outperforming the conventional radiomics model (AUCs: 0.815 and 0.701). Tumor differentiation and neural invasion were identified as independent clinical predictors. The combined model yielded the highest AUCs of 0.956 and 0.881, with favorable calibration and superior net clinical benefit on decision curve analysis (DCA). Conclusions CECT-based habitat radiomics enables robust, non-invasive preoperative prediction of intratumoral TLS in PDAC, offering a practical tool for individualized risk stratification and treatment planning; incorporation of clinical variables yielded numerically higher AUCs but without statistically significant improvement.

title: Dual-energy computed tomography as an alternative to computed tomography perfusion for assessment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis. Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) can quantify tumor hemodynamic parameters. Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) can quantify iodine concentration and may provide perfusion-related information. This study aimed to establish the relationship strength between DECT-derived iodine values and CTP-based parameters in PDAC. This study aimed to establish the relationship strength between DECT derived iodine values and CTP based parameters in PDAC. Methods A total of 47 patients having histologically proven PDAC were enrolled in this study. These patients underwent multi-phase DECT scanning and concurrent dynamic CTP using a single source, fast kVp switching CT scanner. The DECT derived parameters and CTP derived parameters of pancreatic tumor and tumor-free pancreatic parenchyma were calculated, including iodine concentration (IC) and normalized iodine concentration (NIC) in the portal venous and delayed phases, as well as blood flow (BF), blood volume (BV), etc. Statistical different parameters between pancreatic tumor and tumor-free pancreatic parenchyma were analyzed by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves. The diagnostic capability was determined by calculating the area under the curve (AUC). A paired t-test and Pearson correlation were used to evaluate the two techniques. Results For the tumor lesion, IC was 15.21±5.09 and 15.98±4.71 mg/mL in the portal venous and delayed phases, while NIC was 0.31±0.10 and 0.51±0.14. For the tumor-free pancreatic parenchyma, the corresponding values were 27.25±5.43 mg/mL and 21.67±5.23 mg/mL for IC, and 0.55±0.11 and 0.70±0.18 for NIC, respectively. For the tumor lesion, BF and BV were 30.25±11.80 mL/100 g/min and 3.53±2.42 mL/100 g, respectively. For the tumor-free pancreatic parenchyma, BF and BV were 109.74±56.79 mL/100 g/min and 10.77±2.84 mL/100 g, respectively. BF, BV, mean slope of increase (MSI), positive enhancement integral (PEI) and IC in portal venous phase (IC_VP), NIC in portal venous phase (NIC_VP) showed very high diagnostic accuracy (AUC: 0.957-0.981), while IC in delayed phase (IC_DP) and NIC in delayed phase (NIC_DP) demonstrated moderate accuracy. The IC_VP of the tumor lesions showed a moderate positive correlation with BF and BV (r=0.653 and r=0.461, respectively; both P<0.001). The NIC_VP of the tumor lesions also showed a moderate positive correlation with BF and BV (r=0.645 and r=0.491, respectively; both P<0.001). Conclusions In PDAC tumor lesions, DECT derived IC and NIC both show moderate positive correlations with BF and BV, with stronger correlations observed for BF, enabling DECT to evaluate both morphological and perfusion changes.

title: Endoscopic resection of symptomatic lumbar juxtafacet cysts: clinical outcomes, complications, and recurrence in a single-center retrospective study.
abstract: Background Lumbar juxtafacet cysts are degenerative extradural lesions associated with facet arthropathy and segmental instability that may cause radiculopathy, low back pain, neurogenic claudication, and neurological deficit. Full-endoscopic resection may provide direct neural decompression while limiting disruption of posterior stabilizing structures. This study evaluated clinical outcomes, complications, symptomatic recurrence, and patient satisfaction after endoscopic resection of symptomatic lumbar juxtafacet cysts. Methods This single-center retrospective study analyzed prospectively collected data from consecutive adults who underwent endoscopic cyst resection. In patients without motor deficit, surgery was indicated for persistent, functionally limiting symptoms despite at least 3 months of conservative treatment, whereas earlier intervention was considered in patients with motor deficit. Preoperative radiographs were assessed for spondylolisthesis and segmental instability, and isolated endoscopic resection was reserved for patients without an indication for fusion. Clinical outcomes included visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for leg and low back pain and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Complications, symptomatic same-level recurrence, operative time, motor recovery, and patient satisfaction were recorded. Mean follow-up was 19.6 months. Results Twenty-one consecutive patients underwent endoscopic cyst resection; 6 were lost to follow-up, leaving 15 patients for final analysis. Ten patients (66.7%) had no spondylolisthesis or segmental instability, whereas 5 (33.3%) had Meyerding grade I spondylolisthesis. Mean VAS leg pain improved from 7.3±2.79 to 3.8±2.83 (P=0.002), mean VAS low back pain from 7.7±2.87 to 2.1±2.83 (P=0.002), and mean ODI from 42.1±14.55 to 20.7±17.05 (P=0.001). Mean operative time was 110.0±34.4 minutes, and all patients were mobilized on the day of surgery and discharged within 24 hours. One intraoperative dural tear occurred (6.7%) and was repaired endoscopically without postoperative cerebrospinal fluid leakage or further intervention. Increased back pain and leg dysesthesia each occurred in 2 patients (13.3%); these symptoms were managed conservatively and resolved by 6 months. All 4 patients with preoperative motor deficits improved at final follow-up. No symptomatic same-level recurrence was identified. Thirteen patients (86.7%) were satisfied, 11 (73.3%) would recommend the procedure, and 12 (80.0%) would undergo it again if needed. Conclusions In this selected cohort, endoscopic resection was associated with significant improvement in pain and disability, high patient satisfaction, and no symptomatic clinical recurrence at a mean follow-up of 19.6 months. These findings support full-endoscopic resection as a minimally invasive, structure-preserving option in appropriately selected patients. Because of the small sample size and absence of routine postoperative imaging, uncommon complications and asymptomatic radiographic recurrence cannot be excluded. Larger prospective comparative studies with standardized radiographic follow-up are warranted.

title: Computed tomography (CT)-guided fiducial placement for lung nodule localization: a single-center experience.
abstract: Background With the adoption of low-dose computed tomography (CT) for lung cancer screening, small lung nodules are increasingly detected. Sublobar resection has been shown to be oncologically equivalent to lobectomy for peripheral lung cancers ≤2 cm and appropriate for small pulmonary metastases, necessitating localization methods for non-anatomic wedge resection. Preoperative CT-guided metal fiducial placement with intraoperative fluoroscopy is one such method. We hypothesized that this technique would enable high resection success with few complications. Methods We performed a single-institution retrospective review of patients undergoing lung nodule resection preceded by CT-guided fiducial placement between 12/2022-2/2025. Results Fiducial placement was successful in 38 consecutive patients. Complications included hemorrhage [3 (8%), self-limited] and pneumothorax [7 (18%); 3 (8%) requiring pigtail catheter]. All fiducials were identified at the time of surgery. Six nodules could be identified by visualization or palpation alone. Operative plans changed in 3 (8%) cases: one lobectomy after three failed wedge resections, and two cases where the fiducial was not retrieved, but resection was deemed adequate. On final pathology, 29 (76%) patients had adenocarcinoma, 5 (13%) had metastases, and 4 (11%) had non-cancerous lesions. All cancer specimens had negative margins with a median distance to the closest cut margin of 1.4 cm (IQR, 0.7-1.9 cm), and the median lung nodule size was 1.2 cm (IQR, 1.0-1.5 cm). Conclusions CT-guided fiducial placement is a reliable localization method. Pneumothorax requiring intervention occurred in 8% of cases. Nearly all fiducials and suspicious lesions were successfully removed via wedge resection. Compared to other methods of nodule localization, CT-guided fiducial placement was generally well tolerated with a high success rate and few complications, was resource-efficient, and demonstrated prolonged intraparenchymal stability. Further studies, including cost assessments, are needed to compare localization methods.

title: Liposomal bupivacaine versus ropivacaine thoracic paravertebral block for thoracoscopic atrial septal defect repair: analgesic efficacy and cardiac biomarker outcomes in a single-center, assessor-blinded, randomized trial.
abstract: Background Thoracoscopic atrial septal defect (ASD) repair, although minimally invasive, can cause substantial postoperative pain. Thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) provides effective chest wall analgesia, and liposomal bupivacaine (LB), a long-acting local anesthetic with sustained release, may prolong analgesic duration. We investigated whether ultrasound-guided TPVB using long-acting LB improves postoperative analgesia without compromising cardiovascular safety compared with ropivacaine (RP). Methods This randomized, assessor-blinded trial enrolled 94 patients undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, who were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ultrasound-guided TPVB with either LB or RP. Eligibility criteria included age 18-55 years, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) II-III, New York Heart Association (NYHA) II-III, and ejection fraction (EF) >50%. Randomization was computer-generated with sealed envelopes. Safety monitoring included continuous electrocardiography (ECG) for arrhythmias, with Clavien-Dindo grading and Naranjo causality assessment. The primary endpoint was the numerical rating scale (NRS, 0-10) pain score during coughing at 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included NRS scores at other time points, 72-h opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME), time to first rescue analgesia, extended analgesia outcomes [postoperative days 4-7 (POD4-POD7)], perioperative hemodynamics, postoperative recovery, cardiac/inflammatory biomarker trajectories, and adverse events (with postoperative arrhythmias analyzed separately). Results Baseline demographic, clinical, and intraoperative variables were well-balanced between groups (all P>0.05). Compared with RP, LB was associated with lower NRS pain scores at rest and during coughing from extubation through 72 h (all P<0.05), including the primary endpoint at 24 h. LB significantly reduced 72-h opioid consumption [median interquartile range (IQR) 7.5 (0, 42) mg vs. 45 (30, 67.5) mg; P<0.001] and increased the proportion of patients requiring no rescue analgesia within 72 h (72.4% vs. 27.6%; P=0.003). Time to first rescue analgesia was numerically longer with LB (20.5 h vs. 12.0 h; P=0.10), and opioid-sparing effects persisted on POD4-POD7 (both P<0.001). Mechanical ventilation duration was shorter in the LB group [5 (3, 6) h vs. 6 (4, 7.5) h; P=0.03]. Cardiac and inflammatory biomarker trajectories did not differ between groups. Non-arrhythmic adverse events were comparable, and postoperative arrhythmia incidence within 30 days was similar between groups (13.3% vs. 15.6%). Conclusions In adults undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, LB-based TPVB provides superior early analgesia with sustained opioid sparing and shorter mechanical ventilation duration, without signals of increased cardiovascular risk, including postoperative arrhythmias. These findings support considering LB-TPVB as part of multimodal analgesia for thoracoscopic ASD repair, pending confirmation in larger multicenter studies. Trial registration ChiCTR2500112278, retrospectively registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on November 12, 2025.

Secondary outcomes included NRS scores at other time points, 72-h opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME), time to first rescue analgesia, extended analgesia outcomes [postoperative days 4-7 (POD4-POD7)], perioperative hemodynamics, postoperative recovery, cardiac/inflammatory biomarker trajectories, and adverse events (with postoperative arrhythmias analyzed separately).

Results

Baseline demographic, clinical, and intraoperative variables were well-balanced between groups (all P>0.05). Compared with RP, LB was associated with lower NRS pain scores at rest and during coughing from extubation through 72 h (all P<0.05), including the primary endpoint at 24 h. LB significantly reduced 72-h opioid consumption [median interquartile range (IQR) 7.5 (0, 42) mg vs. 45 (30, 67.5) mg; P<0.001] and increased the proportion of patients requiring no rescue analgesia within 72 h (72.4% vs. 27.6%; P=0.003). Time to first rescue analgesia was numerically longer with LB (20.5 h vs. 12.0 h; P=0.10), and opioid-sparing effects persisted on POD4-POD7 (both P<0.001). Mechanical ventilation duration was shorter in the LB group [5 (3, 6) h vs. 6 (4, 7.5) h; P=0.03]. Cardiac and inflammatory biomarker trajectories did not differ between groups. Non-arrhythmic adverse events were comparable, and postoperative arrhythmia incidence within 30 days was similar between groups (13.3% vs. 15.6%).

Conclusions

In adults undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, LB-based TPVB provides superior early analgesia with sustained opioid sparing and shorter mechanical ventilation duration, without signals of increased cardiovascular risk, including postoperative arrhythmias. These findings support considering LB-TPVB as part of multimodal analgesia for thoracoscopic ASD repair, pending confirmation in larger multicenter studies.

title: Development and internal validation of a clinicopathological and CT radiomics based prediction model for extracranial distant metastasis after radical resection in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Background Wide use of low-dose chest CT detects more early NSCLC, though recurrence (mostly extracranial distant metastasis) still occurs. This study aimed to establish and validate computed tomography (CT) radiomics models that can be used for predicting the risk of extracranial distant metastasis (EDM) after radical resection in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (e-NSCLC). Methods This retrospective study included 312 patients with e-NSCLC who underwent radical surgery at Shandong Cancer Hospital from 2014 to 2019. The cases were randomly divided into a training set (n=200) and a validation set (n=112). The study excluded patients who received neoadjuvant therapy, had interrupted follow-up, or died of non-tumor-related causes. The patients were followed up for an average of 30.6 months after the first postoperative CT examination. This study defined EDM as distant metastasis in other organs other than brain metastasis after surgery, and accounted for 78.6% of all metastatic cases. The region of interest (ROI) was delineated, and the radiomics features were selected by using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression models to construct radiomics signatures. The association between the radiomics signature and the occurrence of EDM was also evaluated. A combined nomogram incorporating the selected radiomics and clinical-pathological predictors was constructed using multivariable regression. The concordance index (C-index) was used to evaluate the performance of the model. To determine the clinical effectiveness of nomogram in radiomics, the decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed. Results A total of 75 patients (24.0%) experienced metastasis, with EDM accounting for 78.6%. In the overall cohort, radiomics signature were significantly associated with the occurrence of the EDM. The discrimination performance of the radiomics nomogram is significantly better than the clinical-pathologic nomogram (P<0.001), with the C-indexes 0.818 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.780-0.856] and 0.823 (95% CI: 0.769-0.877) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. Analysis of the calibration and decision curves indicated that the comprehensive nomogram was superior to the clinical-pathological and radiomics nomogram in predicting EDM survival. Conclusions CT radiomics features have the potential to predict postoperative EDM and may assist in preliminarily identifying patients at high metastatic risk, which could provide a reference for individualized postoperative adjuvant decision-making in e-NSCLC.

title: Association between early vein graft failure and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting: an exploratory retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Early vein graft failure (VGF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is far from rare and often clinically silent. While mid-to-late graft failure is established to predict adverse clinical events, the long-term prognostic impact of predischarge early VGF remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between early VGF and 10-year clinical outcomes following off-pump CABG. Methods In this exploratory retrospective cohort study, adult patients undergoing elective isolated off-pump CABG using vein grafts with early postoperative coronary computed tomography angiography between July 2014 and December 2015 were consecutively included. Baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative data were collected from electronic medical records. VGF was defined as Fitzgibbon grade B (≥50% stenosis) or O (occlusion). Patients were stratified into the early VGF group (with at least one failed vein graft) and non-early VGF group (without failed vein grafts). Clinical follow-up was conducted through routine outpatient visits or standardized telephone interviews in accordance with institutional protocol. Primary outcomes included 10-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization) and its individual components. Secondary outcomes included perioperative myocardial injury and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI). Propensity score overlap weighting was applied to adjust for baseline confounders. Exploratory post-hoc landmark and piecewise Cox analyses were performed to address non-proportional hazards. Results A total of 233 patients were included in the analyses (mean age 64.3±7.5 years; 18.4% female). Among them, early VGF was identified in 33 (14.2%) patients and 41 (5.9%) vein grafts. Early VGF numerically increased the risk of perioperative myocardial injury [45.5% vs. 30.5%, odds ratio (OR) 1.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.89-4.01; P=0.09] and PMI (12.1% vs. 6.0%, OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.57-6.69; P=0.21), though without statistical significance. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years, there was no statistically significant difference in 10-year MACE between the two groups [early VGF 51.5% vs. non-early VGF 48.2%; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.31, 95% CI: 0.76-2.24; P=0.33]. In exploratory landmark analyses addressing non-proportional hazards (P=0.03), early VGF was associated with a higher risk of MACE within the first 2 years post-surgery (aHR 2.18, 95% CI: 1.14-4.17; P=0.02), which attenuated beyond the 2-year landmark (aHR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.22-1.46; P=0.24). Additionally, early VGF was associated with a higher risk of repeat revascularization (18.2% vs. 7.7%; aHR 3.06, 95% CI: 1.13-8.31; P=0.03). Conclusions Predischarge early VGF was not significantly associated with the overall 10-year risk of MACE following off-pump CABG. Exploratory findings regarding early risk clustering within 2 years and an increased risk of repeat revascularization remain hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these observations.
