title: Development and internal validation of a chest CT radiomics model for identifying pneumoconiosis.
abstract: Background Pneumoconiosis is a major occupational lung disease with an insidious onset, making early diagnosis challenging. We aimed to develop and internally validate a chest computed tomography (CT)-based radiomics model for objective identification of pneumoconiosis and to support subjective visual diagnosis in dust-exposed individuals. Methods This retrospective study consecutively enrolled 474 patients with documented occupational dust exposure who underwent pneumoconiosis evaluation at The Third People's Hospital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region between January 2020 and December 2024. Eligible participants had high-resolution chest CT images and no history of pulmonary surgery or trauma; those with coexisting respiratory disease, severe systemic dysfunction, or poor image quality were excluded. The reference standard was expert-panel consensus according to GBZ 70-2015 criteria. Lung parenchyma was semi-automatically segmented using a region-growing algorithm in three-dimensional (3D) Slicer, and radiomics features were extracted with the Deepwise Multimodal Research Platform. From 2,153 features, Pearson correlation filtering (r≥0.9 excluded) and analysis of variance (ANOVA) F-test (P<0.05) selected the 10 most discriminative features. Data were randomly divided into training and test sets. A logistic regression model was constructed and evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Of 474 patients, 293 had pneumoconiosis (all stage I) and 181 were dust-exposed controls. The model achieved AUCs of 0.804 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.754-0.853] in the training set (n=331) and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.680-0.838) in the test set (n=143). At the optimal threshold, sensitivity and specificity were 76.2% and 68.3% in the training set and 61.8% and 67.1% in the test set, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and DCA confirmed net clinical benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. Conclusions This CT-based whole-lung radiomics model, without manual lesion delineation, shows promise for early pneumoconiosis identification in dust-exposed populations, with favorable diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility. However, the findings are preliminary and require external validation in independent multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

title: Simplified synchronous division of pulmonary vessels and the horizontal fissure during thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy for lung cancer with incomplete fissure: a propensity score-matched study.
abstract: Background Incomplete horizontal fissure increases the technical difficulty of thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy and may increase parenchymal injury and stapler use. We evaluated a simplified synchronous disconnection of pulmonary vessels and the horizontal fissure (SSDPVH) for right upper lobe non-small cell lung cancer with incomplete fissure. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort included 140 consecutive patients who underwent thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy, including 60 treated with SSDPVH and 80 treated with conventional video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (cVATS). Patients with incomplete or absent horizontal fissure were identified on preoperative high-resolution computed tomography (CT), with final intraoperative confirmation of anatomical suitability. Propensity score matching generated 50 well-balanced pairs. The primary endpoints were operative time, stapler cartridge use, postoperative air leak, and hospitalization cost, reported in Chinese yuan (CNY). Secondary endpoints included blood loss, postoperative stay, nodal yield, perioperative complications, and 18-month follow-up. Results After matching, SSDPVH was associated with shorter operative time [60±5 vs. 74±18 min; mean difference -13 min, 95% confidence interval (CI): -19 to -8; P<0.001] and fewer stapler cartridges (3.8±0.6 vs. 5.6±1.1; mean difference -1.8, 95% CI: -2.1 to -1.5; P<0.001). Total hospitalization cost was lower in the SSDPVH group (32,487±850 vs. 36,145±945 CNY; mean difference -3,658 CNY, 95% CI: -4,022 to -3,294; P<0.001). Prolonged air leak occurred in 2 patients (4.0%) after SSDPVH and 6 patients (12.0%) after cVATS (risk ratio 0.33, 95% CI: 0.07-1.58; P=0.27). Blood loss, postoperative stay, and lymph node harvest were similar between groups. No postoperative bleeding, conversion to open thoracotomy, recurrence, or death was observed in either matched cohort during 18 months of follow-up. Conclusions In this matched retrospective cohort, SSDPVH was associated with shorter operations, fewer stapler reloads, and lower hospitalization cost during thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy for lung cancer with incomplete fissure. The study was not powered to determine differences in postoperative complications or long-term oncologic outcomes.

title: Development and validation of an interpretable clinical-radiomics model for predicting 3-year postoperative recurrence in clinical stage I lung adenocarcinoma: a multicentre study.
abstract: Background Although surgical resection is the standard curative treatment for clinical stage I lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a clinically meaningful proportion of patients still experience postoperative recurrence. Conventional clinical and computed tomography (CT) imaging features have limited ability to provide individualized preoperative risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable CT-based clinical-radiomics model for predicting recurrence within 3 years after surgery in patients with clinical stage I LUAD. Methods This multicentre retrospective prediction model development and validation study included 333 patients with pathologically confirmed clinical stage I LUAD who underwent surgical resection between January 2020 and December 2021. Patients from Center 1 (The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University) (n=199) constituted the training cohort, and those from Center 2 (The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine) (n=134) served as the validation cohort. The outcome was recurrence within 3 years after surgery (determined by imaging findings, clinical follow-up records, and pathological confirmation when available). Patients without recurrence were required to have at least 3 years of follow-up. Radiomics features were extracted from preoperative CT images and selected using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, while clinical predictors were identified using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Radiomics, clinical, and combined models were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the optimal model. Results Overall, 63 of 333 patients (18.9%) experienced recurrence within 3 years after surgery. In the validation cohort, the clinical, radiomics, and combined models achieved the areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.674 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.550-0.799], 0.781 (95% CI: 0.668-0.893), and 0.850 (95% CI: 0.752-0.948), respectively, with corresponding sensitivities/specificities of 0.880/0.385, 0.920/0.532, and 0.840/0.798. The combined model showed significantly better discrimination than the clinical model (DeLong P=0.02). The combined model showed acceptable calibration in the validation cohort, with the calibration intercept, calibration slope, and Brier score were -0.157, 0.763, and 0.114, respectively. DCA suggested a potential net benefit of the combined model across a range of threshold probabilities in both cohorts, while SHAP analysis provided individualized interpretation of model predictions. Conclusions The combined clinical-radiomics model based on preoperative CT and clinical characteristics showed potential for stratifying the risk of recurrence within 3 years after surgery in patients with clinical stage I LUAD. Further validation in larger, prospective cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Prognostic value of changes in skeletal muscle index on serial computed tomography scans for overall survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract: Background Survival rates in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) vary substantially, and changes in host body composition may affect prognosis. Serial computed tomography (CT) can repeatedly quantify skeletal muscle index (SMI) at the L3 level, but its dynamic predictive value and clinically usable thresholds have not been systematically validated. This study systematically evaluates the predictive value of longitudinal SMI changes based on serial CT for overall survival (OS), validate early treatment thresholds, and test its incremental effect over clinical models and Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST). Methods A single-center retrospective cohort was established, including 451 patients with stage IIIB-IV NSCLC who received systemic therapy from 2018 to 2023. L3 SMI was extracted at baseline and follow-up CT; segmentation consistency intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) ≥0.97. ΔSMI% was modeled as a time-dependent exposure (per 5% decrease) in multivariable Cox, and a 12-week landmark analysis was used to evaluate early ΔSMI% ≤-5%. Baseline missing data were handled with MICE (m=20). Combined with RECIST, we compared the C-index, Uno time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), and 12-month net reclassification improvement (NRI), and conducted decision curve analysis and 1,000 bootstrap calibration. Results Each 5% decrease in ΔSMI% was independently associated with increased death risk [hazard ratio (HR) =1.16, P=0.001], and higher baseline SMI was associated with reduced risk (per 10 cm 2 /m 2 HR =0.87, P=0.006); the association between ΔSMI% and death risk was approximately linear (overall P=0.001). At the 12-week landmark analysis, early ΔSMI% ≤-5% was associated with worse survival (log-rank P=0.003), with an adjusted HR =1.68 (P=0.001). The correlation between early ΔSMI% and RECIST was weak (r=-0.18, P=0.001). On top of clinical covariates, adding baseline SMI and time-dependent ΔSMI% increased the corrected C-index from 0.67 to 0.71; 12-month NRI =0.19; AUC at 6/12 months was 0.71/0.70. Decision curves showed higher net benefit than treat all/none within threshold ranges 0.23-0.47 and 0.34-0.58; calibration was good. Conclusions SMI dynamic metrics derived from serial CT constitute an independent and actionable prognostic signal in advanced NSCLC, enable early identification of high-risk patients within routine follow-up windows, and provide incremental gains in discrimination and net benefit over clinical models.

title: Cone-beam computed tomography augmented-fluoroscopy-guided center-strike targeting during peripheral bronchoscopy: robotic vs. manual catheters.
abstract: Background Computed tomography (CT)-to-body divergence and tool-tissue divergence (TTD) limit bronchoscopic access to peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs). Fixed cone-beam CT (CBCT) with augmented fluoroscopy (AF) enables intraprocedural target segmentation, live fluoroscopic overlay, and confirmation of tool position. We describe three CBCT AF-guided spatial targeting techniques as a targeting workflow and compare manual pre-curved and shape-sensing robotic catheters using center strike as the primary technical endpoint. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 200 consecutive patients with 219 biopsied PPLs. The first 100 patients underwent biopsy with manual pre-curved catheters (Medtronic; 106 lesions), followed by 100 patients who underwent biopsy using a shape-sensing robotic catheter (Intuitive; 113 lesions). All procedures used fixed CBCT-AF, a ventilation protocol with apneic breath-holding, needle targeting with traditional two-angle, slow-sweep, and/or center-datum techniques, and CBCT tool-position confirmation. Center strike was defined as needle position in the middle third of the lesion on axial, sagittal, and coronal CBCT images. The primary outcome was center-strike tool position; diagnostic yield and 1-year diagnostic accuracy were secondary outcomes. Results Robotic catheters achieved a higher center-strike rate, the primary endpoint, than manual catheters {66% [75/113; 95% confidence interval (CI): 57-74%] vs. 42% (45/106; 95% CI: 33-52%), P<0.001}, as well as a higher tool-in-lesion (TIL) rate [100% (113/113; 95% CI: 97-100%) vs. 91% (96/106; 95% CI: 83-95%), P<0.001]. Diagnostic yield was 91% (95% CI: 84-95%) vs. 80% (95% CI: 72-87%) (P=0.02), and 1-year diagnostic accuracy was 96% (95% CI: 91-99%) vs. 86% (95% CI: 78-91%) (P=0.01). Dose-area product (DAP) was higher with robotic catheters [median 13,251 [interquartile range (IQR), 8,683-18,264] vs. 11,114 (IQR, 6,336-15,199) µGy·m 2 , P=0.04], without significant differences in fluoroscopy time or number of CBCT spins. Two pneumothoraces occurred in the robotic cohort, one requiring chest tube placement. Conclusions A CBCT AF-guided targeting workflow combines real-time needle-vector alignment with intraprocedural confirmation of tool position before tissue sampling. Within this workflow, robotic catheters achieved higher center-strike and TIL rates and were associated with improved diagnostic performance. Reliable intraprocedural spatial confirmation may become increasingly important as bronchoscopy evolves toward precision transbronchial therapies.

title: Two parallel systems constructed from complementary optical coherence tomography and histopathology for the assessment of murine intestinal inflammation: a dual-modality assessment.
abstract: Background Quantitative assessment of intestinal inflammation among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains a clinical challenge. Conventional histopathology lacks robust quantification, and a real-time, noninvasive alternative is needed. This study aimed to establish a quantitative histopathological system for IBD and to develop a corresponding optical coherence tomography (OCT) system for real-time detection. Methods Murine models for both ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn disease (CD) were developed, and corresponding intestinal histopathological samples were obtained. Artificial intelligence-based image segmentation enabled systematic analysis of pathological images, including two-dimensional planar structures, three-dimensional volumetric morphology, texture features, and grayscale histograms, through which a comprehensive histopathological evaluation system for precise quantitative assessment of intestinal inflammation severity was established. Based on this framework, an OCT system was developed for intestinal wall structural analysis, which demonstrated high concordance with histopathological benchmarks while enabling real-time, noninvasive quantitative detection. Results Both systems effectively differentiated UC, CD, and normal tissue. Planar histopathology revealed significant differences in these models in comparison to controls. The median mucosal fold angle was markedly elevated in UC [median 63.854°, interquartile range (IQR), 37.110-91.151°] and CD (49.925°, IQR, 34.140-62.550°) mice as compared controls (7.635°, IQR, 5.975-10.873°) (both P values <0.001). Submucosal area and cell count were higher in both disease groups, while the gland count was lower (all P values <0.05). Mucosal area ratio decreased from 73.608% in controls to 66.703% in UC mice (P=0.020) and to 59.182% in CD mice (P<0.001), whereas the submucosa ratio increased from 8.127% to 10.812% (P=0.031) and 16.076% (P<0.001), respectively. Three-dimensional reconstruction confirmed increased intestinal wall volumes in both disease groups (all P values <0.05). OCT texture analysis showed decreased energy and increased entropy in the UC and CD groups as compared to the control group (P<0.05), indicating disrupted microstructure. Gray-scale analysis revealed a shift toward lower values in diseased tissues (P<0.001). Pathological texture analysis demonstrated significantly elevated contrast in CD mice (median 153.425) as compared with UC (62.160) and control (70.495) mice (P<0.001), suggesting that CD and UC each have distinct textural signatures. Conclusions This work establishes an integrated framework: a quantitative histopathological system providing novel diagnostic indices, and a complementary OCT system enabling real-time assessment. It offers a proof of concept for multimodal quantitative biomarkers in IBD, an objective tool for preclinical research, and a foundation for future OCT endoscopic applications in clinical evaluation.

title: Atrial and ventricular mechanical dysfunction and myocardial injury predict long-term outcomes in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction is a hallmark of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and imposes chronic pressure overload on the left atrium, leading to progressive atrial remodeling and functional impairment. Conventional left atrial (LA) volumetric indices reflect comparatively advanced structural alterations and are incapable of identifying early functional deterioration. The present research sought to investigate the prognostic significance of LA and LV myocardial deformation parameters obtained from cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with HCM. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 126 HCM patients and 40 healthy volunteers who underwent comprehensive CMR examinations. LA longitudinal strain (reservoir, conduit, and booster components) was assessed using the fast long-axis method; LV global strain and torsion were derived using feature-tracking analysis. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was quantified to assess myocardial fibrosis. Patients with HCM were followed longitudinally for the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of MACEs. Results Compared with healthy volunteers, patients with HCM exhibited significantly impaired LA reservoir, conduit, and booster strain, as well as reduced LV global strain parameters (all P<0.05). Following a median observational period of 1,055 days, 41 patients (32.5%) experienced MACEs. Patients with MACEs demonstrated markedly reduced LA strain and LV torsion compared with those without events. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, LA booster strain [hazard ratio (HR): 0.854, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.799-0.914], LV torsion (HR: 0.517, 95% CI: 0.298-0.895), and serum creatine kinase myocardial band (CKMB) (HR: 1.032, 95% CI: 1.018-1.047) emerged as independent predictors of MACEs. LA booster strain yielded the optimal prognostic efficacy for predicting MACEs [area under the curve (AUC): 0.827]. Conclusions LA booster strain, LV torsion, and CKMB represent complementary markers reflecting atrial function, ventricular mechanics, and myocardial injury, respectively. Their independent associations with adverse outcomes highlight the multifactorial nature of disease progression in HCM and support a more integrative approach to risk stratification beyond single-domain assessment. Incorporating these parameters into routine CMR and clinical evaluation may facilitate earlier identification of patients at increased risk for MACEs and support individualized surveillance strategies.

title: A mathematical framework for pre-mass detection of renal tissue anomalies from computed tomography scans: exploration of a biomechanical signature based on enhancement kinetics.
abstract: Background Early detection of renal cancer remains challenging, as current imaging techniques predominantly identify tumors only after a visible mass has formed. Lesions smaller than 1 cm are particularly difficult to detect reliably using routine computed tomography (CT). This study presents a novel mathematical framework for detecting early renal tissue anomalies before visible mass formation, grounded in the hypothesis that tumorigenesis induces subtle biomechanical alterations in tissue enhancement patterns that are observable on CT imaging. Methods We introduced the Local Biomechanical Index (LBI), a voxel-wise metric quantifying local deviations in Hounsfield unit values relative to an intra-patient renal reference, and a volumetric enrichment ratio (R t/g ) measuring the spatial concentration of extreme LBI values. The single-phase framework was evaluated on a random sample of 20 cases from the KiTS19 dataset using fixed parameters: a 3-mm local radius, the 99th percentile threshold, a 10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm three-dimensional (3D) window, and an enrichment threshold of 2.0. Voxel-level recall, precision, F1-score, and R t/g were calculated against the reference tumor masks and summarized using means, standard deviations (SDs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Across the 20 cases, the mean recall was 0.575 (SD, 0.231; 95% CI: 0.474-0.676), the mean precision was 0.449 (SD, 0.292; 95% CI: 0.321-0.577), and the mean F1-score was 0.431 (SD, 0.221; 95% CI: 0.334-0.528). The mean R t/g was 5.223 (SD, 5.427; 95% CI: 2.842-7.604). Recall exceeded 0.50 in 11 of 20 cases (55%), while R t/g exceeded 2.0 in 14 cases (70%), indicating that candidate anomalies were frequently concentrated within tumor-associated regions. Because KiTS19 provides tumor annotations but does not annotate all other renal abnormalities, the reported precision represents agreement with the reference tumor masks rather than definitive precision for detecting all renal anomalies. Conclusions These findings provide preliminary evidence that early tumor-related biomechanical alterations may be detectable through spatial analysis of enhancement deviations in CT images. The proposed framework operates without tumor segmentation, relies on interpretable statistical measures, and can be fully automated. Although further validation on large longitudinal datasets is required, this approach opens a promising research direction for segmentation-free early detection of renal cancer and for integrating biomechanical signatures into radiological screening workflows.

title: Deep learning-based segmentation, grading and genotype classification of glioma: a literature analysis.
abstract: Background and objective Glioma represents the most prevalent and lethal primary brain tumor in adults, and its high mortality poses a significant challenge to clinical decision-making. While the conventional gold standard for diagnosis relies on the examination of surgically resected tumor tissue, recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have demonstrated compelling performance in medical image analysis, offering the potential for non-invasive prediction of the genetic and histological features of glioma as well as automatic tumor segmentation. This review aims to comprehensively summarize deep learning-based techniques for glioma segmentation, grading, and genotype classification. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) Xplore, and Scopus for articles published in English between January 2014 and December 2025, using combinations of the terms "glioma", "brain tumor", "deep learning", "convolutional neural network", "segmentation", "classification", "grading", "genotype", "isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)", "1p/19q", and "O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT)". Peer-reviewed studies that applied deep learning methods to glioma analysis using medical imaging data and reported quantitative performance results were included, whereas review articles without original results, studies using exclusively non-deep-learning methods, and studies focused solely on non-glioma brain tumors were excluded. Key content and findings This review first summarizes the commonly used public datasets [Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS), The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), synthetic, and private cohorts] and performance metrics, and then surveys deep learning-based approaches for glioma segmentation, grading, and genotype classification according to task. Recent methodological advances, including Vision Transformers, foundation models such as the segment anything model (SAM) and MedSAM, diffusion models, and self-supervised learning, are also discussed. Reported performance varies considerably across datasets and evaluation protocols, and risks of bias, including slice-level data leakage, patient overlap across public repositories, and single-center confounding, remain prevalent in the genotype prediction literature. Conclusions Deep learning has become a transformative tool for non-invasive glioma characterization. Future research should prioritize prospective multi-center validation, standardized evaluation protocols, calibrated uncertainty estimation, and clinically deployable frameworks, thereby facilitating the translation of these techniques into routine diagnostic workflows and ultimately improving outcomes for patients with glioma.

title: Predicting immunotherapy response in patients with non-small cell lung cancer: superior performance of a positron emission tomography radiomics-based stacking ensemble model.
abstract: Background The efficacy of immunotherapy among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) varies, and thus reliable predictive biomarkers of response are needed. This study aimed to develop and validate a stacking ensemble learning model based on pretreatment positron emission tomography (PET) radiomics to predict response to immunotherapy in patients with NSCLC. Methods In this retrospective study, 45 patients with NSCLC treated with immunotherapy were enrolled. Pretreatment Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine-format PET images were preprocessed and normalized. Tumor volumes were segmented using three methods: manual delineation, fixed standardized uptake value (SUV) thresholding with a standardized uptake value of 2.5 (SUV2.5), and adaptive thresholding (40% of the maximum SUV). Radiomics features were extracted, followed by a multistep feature selection process involving mutual information, Spearman correlation, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Predictive models constructed included a stacking ensemble model [with k-nearest neighbors (KNN), logistic regression (LR), and random forest (RF) as base learners], a clinical feature-based model, and a deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated on an independent test set according to the area under the curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Results On the test set, the stacking ensemble model achieved the highest predictive performance using features from the SUV2.5 segmentation dataset, with an AUC of 0.933 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.846-0.994]. This significantly outperformed the best single model (LR; AUC=0.896) and a deep learning model (AUC =0.925). The clinical feature-based model showed moderate predictive capability, with extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) yielding the highest AUC of 0.877 (95% CI: 0.644-1.000). Conclusions The proposed PET radiomics stacking ensemble model, which leverages features from multiple segmentation strategies, demonstrated superior predictive performance for immunotherapy response in NSCLC compared to single models and other benchmarks. This approach offers an effective strategy for enhancing robustness in small-sample radiomics studies and holds promise as a noninvasive decision-support tool that can aid in personalized immunotherapy stratification.

title: Left ventricular function and volumes from cardiac magnetic resonance and gated [ 13 N]-ammonia positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with ischemia with no obstructive coronary arteries: a prospective head-to-head comparison using hybrid positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance.
abstract: Background Electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated 13 N-ammonia positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) has been widely validated for the assessment of left ventricular (LV) volumes and function. This study aimed to compare the accuracy of LV volumes and functional parameters derived from 13 N-ammonia PET with those obtained by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using CMR as the reference standard. Methods A total of 75 consecutive patients with known or suspected ischemia with no obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) who simultaneously underwent ECG-gated 13 N-ammonia PET and CMR using a hybrid PET/magnetic resonance (MR) scanner were enrolled in this prospective study. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), left ventricular end-systolic volume (LVESV), left ventricular stroke volume (LVSV), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and regional wall motion score (RWMS) were derived from both imaging modalities and compared using correlation and Bland-Altman (BA) analyses. Additionally, inter- and intraobserver variability in LV volumetric parameters and LVEF were evaluated for both imaging modalities. Results The correlation between PET and CMR was strong for LV volumes (r>0.83) and moderate for LVEF (r=0.65). The moderate LVEF correlation may be partially explained by the narrow range of LVEF values across the study cohort. Moreover, the agreement between 13 N-ammonia PET and CMR for LVEF was good, with minimal bias (-0.57%); however, 13 N-ammonia PET systematically underestimated LV volumes, with negative biases for LVEDV (-7.76 mL), LVESV (-3.28 mL), and LVSV (-5.33 mL). Similar, strong correlations and good agreement were observed in patients with reduced myocardial flow reserve (MFR). For both PET and CMR, inter- and intraobserver agreement for LV volumes and LVEF was high and comparable between the two modalities. In addition, RWMSs derived from ECG-gated 13 N-ammonia PET and CMR also exhibited good agreement (kappa =0.84±0.02). Conclusions LVEF and RWMS can be reliably and accurately quantified by ECG-gated 13 N-ammonia PET, although LV volumes are systematically underestimated compared with those quantified by CMR. ECG-gated 13 N-ammonia PET may serve as a complementary modality for the assessment of LV systolic function; however, CMR remains the benchmark for LV volumetric measurement and myocardial tissue assessment.

title: Quantification of fat content in the prediction of lymph node metastasis in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a study based on dixon-MRI.
abstract: Background Metastatic tumor infiltration disrupts the normal lymph node (LN) architecture and may result in the loss of the fatty hilum, potentially reducing nodal fat content. The volumetric quantification of nodal fat content using Dixon-magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate Dixon-MRI-derived quantitative nodal fat content in patients with HNSCC and to assess its association with conventional morphological MRI features to develop an integrated predictive model for identifying metastatic LNs. Methods This retrospective study included 101 HNSCC patients with 266 metastatic LNs, as well as 52 age- and sex-matched healthy controls with 172 normal LNs, examined between January 2019 and April 2024. All subjects underwent pretreatment Dixon-MRI examination, and quantitative nodal fat parameters, including volumetric fat signal intensity (vFat SI) and volumetric fat fraction (vFF), as well as conventional morphological MRI features, were quantitatively extracted and analyzed. Comparisons between groups were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or Kruskal-Wallis test. Logistic regression was used to develop predictive models for metastatic LNs, and model performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and area under the curve (AUC). A P value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The HNSCC patient group (median age: 63 years, range: 34-84 years) and control group (median age: 63 years, range: 48-80 years) were analyzed. No significant differences in age and sex were observed between the HNSCC group and the control group (all P>0.05). Metastatic LNs exhibited significantly lower vFat SI (27.50 vs. 51.05, P<0.001) and vFF (6.15 vs. 9.22, P<0.001) compared with normal LNs. Logistic regression analyses indicated that vFF was an independent predictor of metastatic LNs [odds ratio (OR) =0.88, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.78-0.99, P<0.043]. Among the predictive models, the one combining all morphological parameters with vFF achieved the highest AUC (0.910), the sensitivity and specificity were 84.2% and 80.8%, respectively, outperforming the other model (P<0.01 DeLong). Conclusions The quantitative parameters derived from Dixon-MRI have certain value in differentiating the status of cervical LNs in HNSCC, suggesting their potential as an adjunctive imaging biomarker for nodal status assessment.

title: TiLCA-Net: nuclei segmentation and classification in pathological images via task-specialized attention and efficient decoding.
abstract: Background Nuclei segmentation and classification in whole-slide images (WSIs) are critical for tumor diagnosis and treatment. Existing methods often face multi-task feature conflict and computational redundancy. This study aimed to develop an efficient multi-task framework that balances segmentation accuracy and inference efficiency. Methods To seek an improved balance between segmentation accuracy and efficiency, this study proposes TiLCA-Net, a network that integrates multi-scale attention mechanisms with a lightweight decoding strategy to optimize comprehensive model performance. First, a Task-Specialized Attention Integrated Encoder (TSEncoder) is designed to decouple features by assigning spatial, global, and channel attention at multiple levels, thereby mitigating negative transfer. Second, we introduce an iterative cross-enhancement (ICE) module, which utilizes closed-loop iteration and median pooling to enhance global geometric consistency and robustness. Finally, a Lightweight Context Aggregation Decoder (LCA-Decoder) is introduced, replacing redundant structures with multi-scale aggregation to substantially reduce computational cost while preserving high-frequency details. Results Experiments on CoNSeP, MoNuSeg, and CervCell-Seg demonstrate that TiLCA-Net achieves a favorable balance between segmentation performance and computational efficiency. TiLCA-Net achieved mean panoptic quality (PQ) scores of 0.528, 0.578, and 0.592 on CoNSeP, MoNuSeg, and CervCell-Seg, respectively, compared with 0.504, 0.563, and 0.578 for HoVer-Net. These results indicate PQ improvements of 0.024, 0.015, and 0.014 on the three datasets, respectively. Patch-level benchmarking showed that TiLCA-Net required fewer floating point operations per second (FLOPs) and achieved higher batch throughput than HoVer-Net, but with higher single-patch latency and peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory. Conclusions Through feature decoupling and efficient decoder reconstruction, TiLCA-Net provides a practical accuracy-efficiency trade-off for patch-level nuclei analysis in computational pathology.

title: Prediction of late-pregnancy pelvic floor dysfunction: a nomogram model based on proton density fat fraction and synthetic magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: Background Pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) is a highly prevalent condition that significantly compromises women's quality of life. To date, the majority of studies and clinical rehabilitation interventions have focused on the assessment and management of pelvic floor muscle (PFM) function in the postpartum period, whereas investigations into the monitoring of pelvic floor function during the third trimester of pregnancy remain relatively understudied. This study aimed to develop a radiology-clinical nomogram integrating proton density fat fraction (PDFF; Iterative Decomposition of water and fat with Echo Asymmetry and Least-squares estimation, IDEAL-IQ sequence), synthetic magnetic resonance imaging (MAGnetic Resonance Image Compilation, MAGiC sequence), and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) for predicting PFD in late pregnancy. Methods A total of 114 third-trimester pregnant women were classified into PFD and non-PFD groups. Fat fraction (FF), T1, T2, proton density (PD), and fractional anisotropy (FA) of bilateral levator ani muscles (LAMs) were measured from IDEAL-IQ, MAGiC, and DTI by two radiologists (with 15 years of experience). Measurement reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Univariate analysis screened potential predictors [age, gestational week, gravida, parity, delivery mode, fetal weight, pre- and post-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and quantitative imaging parameters]. Significant variables were included in a multivariate logistic regression to build the nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Of 114 participants, 52 were assigned to the PFD group and 62 to the non-PFD group. Univariate analysis showed significant between-group differences in gestational week (P=0.025), gravida (P=0.032), parity (P=0.023), fetal weight (P<0.001), left LAM FF (L-LAM FF, P=0.005), and right LAM T2 (R-LAM T2, P=0.004). The final Akaike information criterion (AIC)-selected multivariable prediction model, gravida, L-LAM FF, and R-LAM T2 were retained as nomogram predictors. The nomogram achieved moderate discrimination with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.726 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.632-0.815]. Calibration indicated good model fit, and DCA demonstrated positive net benefit within a threshold probability range of 25-83%. Interobserver agreement was moderate/excellent (ICC 0.49-0.86). FA was only an exploratory imaging biomarker and was not retained in the final combined prediction model. Conclusions The nomogram incorporating gravida, L-LAM FF, and R-LAM T2 effectively predicts PFD in late pregnancy.

title: The clinical efficacy of magnetic resonance neurography-assisted percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy.
abstract: Background Conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an imaging modality routinely used for the diagnosis of lumbar disc herniation (LDH). Conversely, magnetic resonance neurography (MRN), a novel magnetic resonance (MR)-based technique, has not yet been widely applied in the clinical management of LDH. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of combining MRN with MRI in guiding percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy (PTED) and to explore the potential clinical value of MRN. Methods Patients with LDH who met the inclusion criteria and were admitted to the Department of Orthopedics, Bengbu Third People's Hospital between April 2021 and April 2025 were retrospectively enrolled in the study. A total of 80 patients were included in the study (40 per group) and allocated to a control group (MRI only) and an observation group (MRI combined with MRN) based on whether a preoperative MRN examination was performed. Operative duration, the number of X-ray fluoroscopy sessions, the number of puncture attempts, intraoperative blood loss, and postoperative hospital stay were compared between the groups. Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Japanese Orthopedic Association (JOA) scores were assessed at baseline, on postoperative day 1, and at 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups. Correlations between MRN parameters of the lumbosacral nerve on the affected and unaffected sides and preoperative JOA scores were further analyzed in the observation group. Results We compared the characteristics of the two groups of patients, baseline characteristics, including sex and age, were comparable between the two groups (P>0.05). In the observation group, the morphology and course of the nerve roots were visualized more clearly, providing valuable information for preoperative surgical planning. The observation group exhibited superior outcomes in terms of operative duration, the number of X-ray fluoroscopy sessions, the number of puncture attempts, and intraoperative blood loss compared with the control group (P<0.01); however, no significant difference in postoperative hospital stay was observed (P>0.05). Lower VAS scores were observed in the observation group at the 12-month postoperative follow-up, while higher JOA scores were observed at the 3-, 6-, and 12-month postoperative follow-ups (P<0.001). Significant differences in nerve root diameter, dorsal root ganglion length, and signal intensity were detected between the affected and unaffected sides in the observation group (P<0.05). Further, the difference in signal intensity was significantly correlated with the preoperative JOA score (r=0.721, P<0.001). Conclusions Preoperative MRN examination may facilitate preoperative assessment and surgical planning compared with conventional imaging modalities. The inter-side differences in MRN signal intensity parameters between the affected and unaffected sides, together with their observed correlations with JOA scores, provide preliminary evidence of the potential prognostic value of MRN.

title: Fully automatic airway segmentation in CT images via dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion.
abstract: Background Precise segmentation of airways from computed tomography (CT) images is critical for pre-procedural planning in navigational bronchoscopy; however, existing methods often suffer from distal branch fractures and morphological losses due to slender diameters, low contrast, and noise. To address these limitations and achieve accurate, topologically complete airway segmentation, this study proposed a novel dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion. Methods A two-stage centerline-guided network (TSC-Net) was developed that innovatively combines centerline structural similarity (CSS) loss and centerline overlap rate (COR) loss. CSS loss maintains the continuity of airway tree structures by strengthening centerline morphological constraints, while COR loss enhances global centerline overlap to ensure branch integrity. Additionally, a topology-difference-driven fracture-region completion mechanism was adopted to adaptively repair the fracturedand misclassified areas. The model employs a residual UNet (ResUNet) backbone integrated with an atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module to capture multi-scale contextual features and adopts a two-stage training strategy in which the encoder is frozen during stage 2 while the decoder is fine-tuned using dynamically adjusted loss weights. This strategy enables targeted optimization of discontinuous regions without compromising globally well-predicted areas. Results Experiments on the Airway Tree Modeling Challenge 2022 (ATM'22), Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI), Extraction of Airways from CT (EXACT'09), and private datasets showed that TSC-Net achieved a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 93.2%±2.1%, significantly outperforming SwinUNETR (92.9%±3.6%, P<0.05), nnUNet (91.2%±1.2%, P<0.05), and UNet (75.6%±4.3%, P<0.05). The tree-length detection (TD) rate reached 95.5%±4.2%, and the branch detection (BD) rate reached 92.6%±3.6%, both of which were significantly higher than those of all baseline methods (P<0.01). Moreover, the segmented distal branches exhibited continuous and smooth morphology. Conclusions Overall, our method significantly enhanced both segmentation accuracy and distal branch integrity in automated CT-based airway segmentation through multi-dimensional feature enhancement, topological constraint optimization, and a dynamic completion mechanism. This method holds great promise for pre-procedural planning in robotic-assisted bronchoscopy by enabling accurate visualization of peripheral airways and facilitating navigation to distant pulmonary targets.

title: Structural alterations in the superior temporal gyrus associated with depressive symptoms in migraine without aura: a voxel-based morphometry and surface-based morphometry magnetic resonance imaging study.
abstract: Background Migraine without aura (MwoA) frequently co-occurs with depressive symptoms, yet the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this comorbidity remain insufficiently characterized. This study integrated voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and surface-based morphometry (SBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) and cortical morphology between patients with MwoA and healthy controls (HC) and to further determine whether structural brain alterations vary across MwoA subgroups stratified by depressive symptom severity, thereby identifying potential structural correlates of depressive symptoms in this population. Methods A total of 67 patients with MwoA {38 with lower depressive symptoms [MwoA-LS, 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) <8] and 29 with higher depressive symptoms (MwoA-HS, HAMD-17 ≥8)} and 40 HC were included. High-resolution T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data were processed using CAT12 to derive GMV, cortical thickness (CT), local gyrification index (LGI), sulcal depth (SD), and fractal dimension (FD). Between-group comparisons were conducted using two-sample t-tests within a general linear model framework, with sex, education, total intracranial volume (TIV) (for VBM), mean CT (for SBM), and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA) scores included as covariates. Statistical significance was defined using a voxel-/vertex-level threshold of P<0.001 (uncorrected), followed by cluster-level false discovery rate (FDR) correction at q<0.05. Results Compared with HC, patients with MwoA exhibited significant reductions in GMV in the left amygdala (cluster size =305; FDR-corrected q=0.046), left parahippocampal gyrus (cluster size =273; q=0.036), left lingual gyrus (two clusters, size =218, q=0.046 and size =177, q=0.046), and right angular gyrus extending into the middle occipital gyrus and precuneus (cluster size =427; q=0.036). No significant between-group differences were observed in any SBM measure. In the subgroup analysis, patients in the MwoA-HS group showed significantly lower LGI in the right superior temporal gyrus than those in the MwoA-LS group (cluster size =73; FDR-corrected q=0.019). Exploratory partial correlation analyses indicated that no imaging metric was significantly associated with HAMD-17 scores or other clinical measures after FDR correction (all q>0.05). Conclusions Patients withMwoA exhibited widespread GMV reductions across brain regions involved in emotional and pain-related processing. In addition, patients with higher depressive symptom levels showed a distinct cortical morphological feature characterized by lower LGI in the right superior temporal gyrus, which was not detected by VBM. Given the exploratory nature of these findings, the lack of significant brain-clinical correlations after correction for multiple comparisons, and the cross-sectional study design, these results should be validated in larger longitudinal cohorts.

title: Gadoxetic acid in China: a narrative review of the 15-year journey and the road ahead.
abstract: Background and objective Since its pivotal introduction in 2011, gadoxetic acid has fundamentally revolutionized the landscape of hepatobiliary imaging in China, shifting the diagnostic paradigm from morphological assessment toward functional hepatocyte-level evaluation. This review comprehensively summarizes its 15-year clinical evolution within the Chinese healthcare system, exploring its pharmacological benefits, advanced applications, and future integration with data-driven frameworks. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, spanning from 2011 to 2026. The search targeted peer-reviewed articles, consensus statements, clinical guidelines, and high-impact reviews published in English and Chinese regarding gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Key content and findings Gadoxetic acid provides high sensitivity for early small hepatocellular carcinoma (sHCC) detection via specific OATP1B3 uptake. Beyond lesion detection, its quantitative mapping shows potential for estimating hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and risk stratification for post-hepatectomy liver failure. Crucially, the ongoing paradigm shift toward integrating radiomics and deep learning bridges macroscopic imaging and microscopic molecular biology, theoretically enabling a multi-dimensional profile of liver parenchyma and lesions within a single diagnostic session. However, a significant gap remains between retrospective predictive performance and clinical readiness, and these data-driven frameworks currently serve as supplementary investigational engines rather than standalone clinical decision-makers. Moving forward, integrating these high-dimensional signatures into constructs such as "digital twin" represents the next frontier. Furthermore, China's hepatitis B virus-dominant epidemiological cohorts, comprehensive multi-modal datasets, "Med-Engineering" fusion, and collaborative networks uniquely accelerate the development and preliminary validation of these models, offering valuable insights for global precision hepatology within China's healthcare system. Conclusions Over the past 15 years, gadoxetic acid has evolved far beyond a conventional liver imaging tool in China. While clinical translation of advanced analytics requires rigorous, prospective multicenter validation to ensure safety, combining this functional imaging agent with data-driven frameworks represents a promising frontier to eventually optimize future radiology workflows and support personalized precision hepatology.

title: Image quality and radiation dose optimization in CT pulmonary angiography using 120, 100, and 80 kV protocols for pulmonary thromboembolism diagnosis.
abstract: Background Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is the standard imaging modality for diagnosing pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE). Lowering tube potential enhances iodine attenuation but may affect image noise. This retrospective study evaluated quantitative image quality, subjective ratings, and radiation dose across 120, 100, and 80 kV CTPA protocols on a dual-source CT scanner. Methods Ninety adult patients (n=30 per protocol) undergoing clinically indicated CTPA were evaluated across three tube potential settings (120, 100, and 80 kV). Quantitative parameters pulmonary artery attenuation [Hounsfield unit (HU)], image noise [standard deviation (SD)], signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and size-specific dose estimates (SSDE)-were evaluated. Three cardiothoracic radiologists performed blinded qualitative assessments using a 5-point Likert scale. Radiation dose metrics [volumetric computed tomography dose index (CTDIvol), dose-length product (DLP), and estimated effective dose] were recorded. Results Baseline characteristics [age, sex, body mass index (BMI)] were comparable across groups (P>0.05). Pulmonary artery attenuation increased significantly as tube potential decreased, reaching highest values at 80 kV (633.9±92.1 vs. 338.5±42.1 HU at 120 kV, P<0.001). Image noise increased modestly at 80 kV (25.88±5.0 vs. 20.23±4.1 HU, P=0.26). SNR and CNR were significantly higher at 80 kV (25.93±2.6 and 25.20±3.4) compared with 120 kV (18.19±4.8 and 9.31±2.1, P<0.001). Effective dose decreased significantly by 46.4% from 3.34±0.67 mSv (120 kV) to 1.79±0.35 mSv (80 kV) (P<0.001). Qualitative scores for overall image quality, vascular enhancement, and motion artifacts showed no significant differences across protocols (P>0.05). Conclusions Lowering tube potential to 80 kV in CTPA significantly increases vascular attenuation, SNR, and CNR while offering substantial radiation dose savings and maintaining subjective image quality scores. These findings support the feasibility of an 80-kV protocol for radiation dose optimization in CTPA.

title: Incremental prognostic and risk-stratification value of ultrasound-based Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) classification for recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.
abstract: Background The Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) is a system for stroke risk assessment. However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis. Methods Between January 2020 and December 2022, 231 patients with carotid plaque ipsilateral to the prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis were retrospectively screened, of whom 158 were included in the final analysis. US-based Plaque-RADS classification was assigned based on duplex US assessment of plaque features. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories and recurrent ischemic stroke. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC), and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis. The association between increasing US-based Plaque-RADS categories and the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke was assessed by trend analysis. The incremental risk-stratification value of refined high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds was quantified with net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. Results During the 3-year follow-up period, recurrent ischemic stroke occurred in 33 patients. High-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, after adjusting for smoking, homocysteine, and intraplaque neovascularization [adjusted hazard ratio: 3.56; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-11.83, P=0.038]. No statistically significant interactions were observed across the subgroups (all P for interaction >0.05). The Plaque-RADS ≥3 model demonstrated a higher AUC than the conventional US model [0.816 (95% CI: 0.731-0.901) vs. 0.810 (95% CI: 0.720-0.899)] and provided a slight net benefit across selected threshold probabilities. Additionally, the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke increased with higher Plaque-RADS categories (P for trend <0.001). Among the models using different high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds, the Plaque-RADS ≥3b model showed the best predictive performance (0.865, 95% CI: 0.799-0.930), compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model and the Plaque-RADS ≥3c model [0.824 (95% CI: 0.740-0.906)]. The Plaque-RADS ≥3b model also showed moderate improvements in NRI [0.250; (95% CI: 0.088-0.557), P=0.017] and IDI [0.090; (95% CI: 0.000-0.185), P=0.049], compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model. Bootstrap internal validation indicated limited optimism across all models. Conclusions In patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke. The US-based Plaque-RADS may help identify plaque phenotypes associated with an increased risk of recurrent ipsilateral ischemic stroke, while refined high-risk thresholds, particularly Plaque-RADS ≥3b, may provide additional value for risk stratification.

title: Artificial intelligence applications in photon-counting detector CT for coronary artery disease imaging: a narrative review.
abstract: Background and objective Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a first-line non-invasive imaging modality for CAD evaluation, but conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) is often limited by blooming artifacts, noise, and partial-volume effects. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) provides superior spatial resolution, reduced blooming, and multi-energy spectral data, yet its ultra-high-resolution (UHR) datasets frequently suffer from increased noise and complex spectral information that require advanced processing. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising solution to fully exploit PCD-CT's advantages. This narrative review aims to synthesize the current evidence on AI applications in PCD-CT for CAD imaging, evaluate their technical performance and clinical potential, identify limitations, and propose future directions. Methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase, supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. Original English-language studies applying AI techniques to PCD-CT data for CAD imaging were included, and categorized using a 5-level translational framework. Key content and findings Thirty single-center studies were identified and grouped into three main categories. In image quality improvement, denoising models achieved 60-96% noise reduction while preserving spatial and spectral fidelity. Radiomics studies (the largest group) identified specific texture features in myocardium, plaques, pericoronary, and epicardial adipose tissue associated with coronary artery calcium severity, hypercholesterolemia, aging, and CAD presence, although feature reproducibility was only moderate. Automated detection/quantification/segmentation tools demonstrated high reproducibility, improved stenosis quantification, substantial workflow benefits, and promising CT-fractional flow reserve (FFR) performance with strong intra-individual agreement to EID-CT. Conclusions AI has shown promising technical advancements when applied to PCD-CT for CAD imaging. However, the evidence base remains limited by small sample sizes, single-center and single-scanner designs, lack of external validation, and absence of outcome-driven studies. Future research should focus on multicenter prospective validation, standardized protocols, human-in-the-loop systems, and clinical impact assessment to support the safe and effective translation of AI-enhanced PCD-CT into routine clinical practice.

title: Combined quantitative speed-of-sound imaging and shear-wave elastography for differentiating benign and malignant breast lesions: development of a multimodal ultrasound nomogram.
abstract: Background Accurate differentiation of benign and malignant breast lesions is essential for guiding clinical management and reducing unnecessary biopsies. However, conventional ultrasound alone often has limited specificity. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of shear-wave elastography (SWE) and quantitative speed-of-sound (QSOS) imaging and to develop a multimodal ultrasound nomogram integrating quantitative imaging parameters with conventional ultrasound features for breast lesion characterization. Methods This retrospective study included 108 breast lesions (43 malignant and 65 benign) from 108 women who underwent conventional B-mode ultrasound, SWE, and QSOS imaging before histopathological confirmation. Quantitative SWE and QSOS parameters were obtained from intralesional and perilesional regions. Imaging predictors associated with malignancy were selected through least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and subsequently evaluated using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Independent predictors were incorporated into a diagnostic nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, DeLong test, calibration curves, bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions) for internal validation, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Malignant lesions exhibited significantly higher maximum elasticity (E max ) and QSOS values than benign lesions [E max : 70.6±33.5 vs. 40.9±21.4 kPa; QSOS: 1,557.1 (1,535.8-1,564.9) vs. 1,529.7 (1,506.1-1,543.9) m/s; both P<0.001]. Multivariable analysis identified lesion size [odds ratio (OR) =1.12, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.02-1.26, P=0.030], non-parallel orientation (OR =18.93, 95% CI: 2.00-303.26, P=0.019), calcification (OR =20.18, 95% CI: 3.44-187.76, P=0.002), E max (OR =1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.10, P=0.007), and QSOS per 10 m/s increase (OR =1.71, 95% CI: 1.13-2.93, P=0.024) as independent predictors of malignancy. QSOS and E max showed moderate diagnostic performance, with areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.776 and 0.775, respectively, whereas their combination improved the AUC to 0.850 (95% CI: 0.774-0.926). The multimodal nomogram integrating conventional ultrasound features, E max , and QSOS achieved excellent discrimination (AUC =0.969; 95% CI: 0.943-0.994), with 88.4% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity. The nomogram significantly outperformed the conventional ultrasound model alone according to the DeLong test (P=0.030) and demonstrated favorable calibration and clinical utility. Conclusions SWE and QSOS provide complementary quantitative information for breast lesion characterization. Integration of conventional ultrasound features with quantitative stiffness and sound-speed information in a multimodal nomogram demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance and may provide a quantitative adjunctive approach for improving breast lesion assessment and clinical decision-making.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound-based imaging modalities for assessing residual axillary lymph node disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Accurate identification of residual axillary lymph node (ALN) disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is essential for treatment planning and for evaluating potential surgical de-escalation. We assessed the diagnostic performance of conventional ultrasonography (US), shear-wave elastography (SWE), artificial intelligence (AI)/radiomics, and multimodal ultrasound-based models for post-NAC axillary restaging. Methods PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through December 2025. Histopathology after axillary surgery was the reference standard, and residual axillary nodal disease (ypN+) was uniformly defined as the positive target condition. Study-level 2×2 tables were harmonized to this direction. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Bivariate random-effects models and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves were used for modality groups with a sufficient number of independent studies; the positive likelihood ratio (PLR) and negative likelihood ratio (NLR) were pooled with random-effects models. Potentially overlapping cohorts were examined in sensitivity analyses. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; registration No. CRD420251271199). Results A total of 14 articles were included in the systematic review, 10 of which contributed 12 test-level datasets to the quantitative synthesis. For conventional US (six studies), the pooled sensitivity was 0.55 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.36-0.73], the pooled specificity was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.73-0.84), the area under the HSROC curve (AUC) was 0.78, and the pooled PLR and NLR were 2.47 (95% CI: 1.42-4.28) and 0.54 (95% CI: 0.30-0.95), respectively. AI/radiomics models (three studies) showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.80-0.98), a specificity of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.60-0.94), and an AUC of 0.94; however, likelihood-ratio CIs were wide, and the bivariate covariance estimate reached the boundary. Evidence for SWE was limited to two potentially overlapping reports, and only one multimodal combined-model study had a complete harmonized 2×2 table. At a 40% pretest probability, a negative conventional US result reduced the posttest probability of residual nodal disease to approximately 26%. Conclusions Conventional US alone does not reliably exclude residual axillary nodal disease after NAC. AI/radiomics approaches show promising diagnostic performance, but the evidence for this is sparse, heterogeneous, and imprecise. The currently available data do not support definitive modality ranking or omission of axillary surgery on the basis of imaging alone, and prospective multicenter external validation is required.

For conventional US (six studies), the pooled sensitivity was 0.55 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.36-0.73], the pooled specificity was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.73-0.84), the area under the HSROC curve (AUC) was 0.78, and the pooled PLR and NLR were 2.47 (95% CI: 1.42-4.28) and 0.54 (95% CI: 0.30-0.95), respectively. AI/radiomics models (three studies) showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.80-0.98), a specificity of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.60-0.94), and an AUC of 0.94; however, likelihood-ratio CIs were wide, and the bivariate covariance estimate reached the boundary. Evidence for SWE was limited to two potentially overlapping reports, and only one multimodal combined-model study had a complete harmonized 2×2 table. At a 40% pretest probability, a negative conventional US result reduced the posttest probability of residual nodal disease to approximately 26%.

Conclusions

Conventional US alone does not reliably exclude residual axillary nodal disease after NAC. AI/radiomics approaches show promising diagnostic performance, but the evidence for this is sparse, heterogeneous, and imprecise. The currently available data do not support definitive modality ranking or omission of axillary surgery on the basis of imaging alone, and prospective multicenter external validation is required.

title: Development and internal validation of transrectal ultrasound radiomics models for patient- and needle-level prostate cancer prediction in biopsy-naive men.
abstract: Background Current prostate cancer (PCa) assessment uses clinical findings, prostate-specific antigen (PSA), and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mp-MRI), while transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) mainly provides real-time biopsy guidance. We developed zone-specific TRUS radiomics models for patient-level and planned needle-level PCa prediction. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 247 biopsy-naive men undergoing freehand transperineal 10-core systematic biopsy from August 2023 to April 2024. Each patient contributed two transition zone (TZ) cores and eight peripheral zone (PZ) cores. A blinded sonographer delineated whole-zone and pre-firing needle-target regions of interest (ROIs), visually matched to post-firing images acquired seconds later. From each ROI, 513 radiomic features were extracted, sparsely selected, and classified with a two-layer RNN. Models were evaluated using an 80:20 split. A patient or core was positive when pathology showed Gleason score (GS) ≥6. Results The cohort included 116 patients with PCa and 131 with benign findings; 545 of 2,470 cores were positive. Without PSA, the combined TZ + PZ patient-level model had the highest patient-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) (0.828), whereas needle-level AUCs were 0.699, 0.698, and 0.680 for TZ, PZ, and TZ + PZ models. With PSA, the combined patient-level model reached an AUC of 0.876, and the needle-level TZ + PSA model reached 0.826. Conclusions The findings support further investigation of zone-specific TRUS radiomics, particularly for patient-level prediction. Needle-level results are exploratory and do not establish real-time biopsy guidance. External validation, confidence intervals, comparator models, prospective registration, and patient-grouped evaluation are required before clinical use.

title: A multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging-based composite index for non-invasive discrimination of breast cancer molecular subtypes.
abstract: Background Breast cancer exhibits high molecular heterogeneity, with significant differences in biological behavior, treatment response, and prognosis across molecular subtypes. Current molecular subtyping relies on immunohistochemistry or in situ hybridization of biopsy or surgical specimens; however, intratumoral heterogeneity may introduce sampling bias and lead to inaccurate subtyping. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mp-MRI) can non-invasively capture the overall biological characteristics of tumors, offering a potential complementary approach for preoperative molecular subtyping. Nevertheless, the value of integrating multiple MRI parameters reflecting both cellular structure and vascular function for distinguishing key molecular subtypes remains to be further explored. Accordingly, this study aimed to evaluate differences in apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) heterogeneity and dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) kinetic parameters among key molecular subtypes and to develop and internally validate a composite mp-MRI index for discriminating these subtypes, with a primary focus on distinguishing the Luminal subtype from triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 172 patients with pathologically confirmed invasive breast cancer, who were classified into Luminal (94 cases), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-overexpressing (34 cases), and TNBC (44 cases) subtypes based on immunohistochemistry. Preoperative breast mp-MRI was performed on all patients, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and DCE-magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). ADC heterogeneity, DCE semi-quantitative parameters, and morphological features were extracted. Differences in these parameters were compared among the three groups. Binary logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors and to construct a composite index, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results When comparing the Luminal subtype with TNBC, the Luminal subtype exhibited significantly lower ADC heterogeneity, relative enhancement (RE), and wash-out rate (WOR), and significantly higher time to peak (TTP) and wash-in rate (WIR) (all P<0.05). Multivariate analysis revealed that ADC heterogeneity [odds ratio (OR) =0.002], TTP (OR =1.016), and WOR (OR =0.206) were independent predictors, and the composite index, derived from these predictors, yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.915. When comparing the HER2-overexpressing subtype with TNBC, neither ADC heterogeneity nor TTP demonstrated independent predictive value. When comparing the Luminal subtype with the HER2-overexpressing subtype, multivariate analysis identified only WOR (OR =0.313) as an independent predictor. Conclusions The integration of ADC heterogeneity and DCE kinetic parameters in mp-MRI effectively reflects the biological differences among major molecular subtypes of breast cancer. The multiparametric composite index based on ADC heterogeneity, TTP, and WOR demonstrates excellent diagnostic performance in distinguishing Luminal subtype from TNBC, providing a reliable imaging approach for preoperative non-invasive molecular subtyping.

title: Development and validation of a phase-stable computed tomography radiomics model for brain metastasis risk stratification in non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Background Brain metastasis (BM) is a frequent complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but individualized risk stratification remains limited. We evaluated whether computed tomography (CT) radiomic features reproducible across non-enhanced and contrast-enhanced phases could improve BM risk prediction and whether integration with clinical biomarkers and semantic CT findings provided additional value. Methods This retrospective study included 226 patients with pathologically confirmed NSCLC who underwent pretreatment multiphase chest CT and contrast-enhanced brain magnetic resonance imaging. BM was defined as metastasis detected at baseline or during follow-up. Patients were randomly divided into training (n=181) and held-out test (n=45) sets. Radiomic features reproducible between non-contrast-enhanced CT (NE-CT) and venous-phase contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) were defined as phase-stable using an intraclass correlation coefficient greater than 0.80. Radiomic features were reduced using univariable filtering, correlation analysis, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) with 5-fold cross-validation. Clinical biomarkers and semantic CT features were integrated with phase-stable radiomics. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), classification metrics, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results Among single-sequence models, NE-CT showed the best discrimination (AUC, 0.901; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.858-0.945 in training and 0.765; 95% CI: 0.618-0.912 in testing). The phase-stable radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.832 (95% CI: 0.773-0.891) and 0.793 (95% CI: 0.657-0.929), respectively. Adding clinical biomarkers improved test performance (AUC, 0.909), whereas further addition of semantic CT findings yielded similar discrimination (AUC, 0.908). The fully combined model had test accuracy of 0.867, sensitivity of 0.667, specificity of 0.939, positive predictive value of 0.800, and negative predictive value of 0.886. Within thin-slice CT protocols of 2 mm or less, differences in contrast phase and reconstruction kernel had limited influence on model discrimination. Conclusions Phase-stable CT radiomics provided reproducible BM risk stratification in NSCLC. Integration with clinical biomarkers improved discrimination, whereas semantic CT findings provided limited additional gain. These findings support further multicenter validation of phase-stability-guided CT radiomics for BM risk assessment.

title: Predictive performance of diffusion kurtosis imaging combined with magnetic resonance imaging morphological features for MGMT promoter status in glioma.
abstract: Background Gliomas with O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter (MGMTp)-methylation exhibit superior therapeutic responses, as well as longer progression-free survival and overall survival. Diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) is an extension of diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) that quantifies the degree of non-Gaussian diffusion of water molecules. This provides superior sensitivity to the complex microstructural heterogeneity of brain tumors. This study aimed to explore the diagnostic performance of DKI combined with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) morphological features in predicting the 6 -methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter (MGMTp) status in gliomas. Methods Sixty-one patients with glioma who underwent biopsy or surgery were included, comprising 39 cases in the MGMTp-methylated group and 22 cases in the MGMTp-unmethylated group. All patients underwent conventional MRI and DKI sequences preoperatively. This study quantified DKI metrics in the tumor region and in contralateral normal-appearing white matter (NAWM). Subsequently, relative DKI parameters were calculated for both the tumor parenchyma and the peritumoral edema region. These included relative mean kurtosis (rMK), relative radial kurtosis (rKr), relative axial kurtosis (rKa), relative mean diffusivity (rMD), and relative fractional anisotropy (rFA). Differences in clinical data, morphological features, and DKI-derived parameters were compared between the two groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were utilized to determine the diagnostic performance, including the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results Among 61 patients, 39 (63.9%) had MGMTp methylation. MGMTp methylation was significantly associated with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status (P=0.001). Blurred tumor margins were more frequent in methylated gliomas (71.8% vs. 18.2%, P<0.001). In the tumor parenchyma, the unmethylated group showed significantly higher rMK and rKr, and lower rMD (all P<0.001). Multivariable analysis confirmed that rMK [odds ratio (OR) =0.12, P = 0.003], rMD (OR =4.85, P = 0.02), and blurred margins (OR =6.42, P = 0.009) remained independent predictors after adjusting for World Health Organization (WHO) grade and IDH status. The fusion model combining rMK and tumor margin achieved the highest AUC of 0.924 (sensitivity 87.8%, specificity 81.8%). Normalization significantly and critically enhances the predictive performance for MGMTp methylation status. Conclusions DKI parameters, particularly rMK and rMD, combined with MRI morphological features (blurred tumor margin), provide excellent non-invasive prediction of MGMTp methylation status in gliomas, independent of tumor grade and IDH mutation status. This integrative approach may facilitate preoperative treatment planning and individualized chemotherapy strategies.
