title: Development and Validation of a Feature-Prompted Deep Learning System for Diagnosing Chronic Atrophic Gastritis Under White-Light Endoscopy
abstract: Abstract Background Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous condition whose endoscopic detection under white-light endoscopy (WLE) is limited by low sensitivity and high inter-observer variability. We aimed to develop and validate an end-to-end artificial intelligence (AI) system for CAG diagnosis during WLE and compare it with endoscopists of different experience levels. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective study in which an AI system with three sequential deep learning modules (image quality assessment, anatomical site classification, and atrophy detection) was trained and validated on data from 943 patients. The atrophy detection module used a feature-prompted strategy: segmentation masks were applied to focus the classifier on suspected atrophic regions. The best model was compared with six endoscopists (four intermediate, two senior) on an independent test set, with histopathology as the reference standard. Results The feature-prompted model (DCNN3a-1) reached a sensitivity of 92.4%, specificity of 89.2%, and accuracy of 90.9%. Its accuracy was not significantly different from that of senior endoscopists (90.9% vs. 90.3%, p = 0.738) but was higher than that of intermediate endoscopists (85.6%, p < 0.001) and the overall endoscopist group (87.2%, p < 0.05). Conclusions The AI system achieves expert-level CAG diagnostic performance under WLE. The feature-prompted approach improves accuracy over whole-image classification and may help standardize CAG diagnosis in routine clinical practice.

title: Risk Factors for Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis and a Predictive Model for Lateral Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is the most common thyroid malignancy. Although the overall prognosis is favorable, cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) occurs in a substantial proportion of patients and affects both surgical planning and clinical outcomes. Preoperative ultrasonography remains limited in sensitivity, particularly for occult metastases, and existing predictive tools rarely distinguish between central and lateral compartments. A dedicated model for lateral cervical lymph node metastasis (LC-LNM) is therefore needed. Methods: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 450 patients with newly diagnosed PTC who underwent thyroid surgery between January 2022 and December 2024. Clinicopathological characteristics, BRAF V600E mutation status, preoperative ultrasound features, and surgical data were collected. Variables associated with central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) and LC-LNM were identified by univariate analysis and entered into multivariable binary logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit testing, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: Tumor maximum diameter, BRAF V600E mutation, calcification, and male sex were significantly associated with CLNM. For LC-LNM, tumor diameter, BRAF V600E mutation, calcification, a taller-than-wide shape (aspect ratio >1), tumor laterality (unilateral vs. bilateral), and an indistinct tumor margin were identified as independent correlates. In the resulting LC-LNM model, tumor diameter, BRAF V600E mutation, calcification, and aspect ratio >1 were positive predictors, whereas unilateral lesions and a clear tumor margin were negative predictors. The model showed good fit (Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.526) and an AUC of 0.863. Calibration was high (MAE = 0.016; MSE < 0.001; 90th percentile absolute error = 0.055), and DCA indicated net clinical benefit across a threshold probability range of 0.05–0.65. Conclusion: LNM in PTC is associated with a distinct set of clinicopathological factors in the central and lateral compartments. The proposed LC-LNM model integrates readily available preoperative clinical, ultrasound, and molecular variables and may serve as a quantitative adjunct to guide individualized decision-making regarding lateral neck dissection.

title: Oral lichen planus in a patient with neurofibromatosis type 1: the first biopsy- confirmed case report
abstract: Abstract Oral lichen planus co-occurring with neurofibromatosis type 1 is exceptionally rare. A comprehensive literature search revealed no prior reports of biopsy-confirmed OLP in NF1 patients. This report describes the first such case in a 22-year-old woman with familial NF1 confirmed by whole exome sequencing (pathogenic variant: c.2850 + 1delG). The patient presented with a 6-month history of intermittent burning and discomfort in the buccal mucosa during orthodontic treatment. Clinical examination showed bilateral reticular white striae with erythematous erosions on the buccal mucosa, alongside classic NF1 features including multiple café-au-lait macules and neurofibromas. Differential diagnoses such as lichenoid reaction to amalgam, systemic lupus erythematosus, and drug-induced lichenoid reaction were excluded based on the absence of any amalgam restorations, negative serological tests for autoimmune markers (including ANA and anti-dsDNA), lack of systemic symptoms suggestive of SLE, and no history of medications associated with lichenoid reactions. The diagnosis of erosive OLP was clinicopathologic, supported by histopathology revealing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, basal keratinocyte necrosis, and Civatte bodies. Treatment included incisional biopsy and topical triamcinolone acetonide 0.1%, resulting in complete resolution of lesions and symptoms within one month. No recurrence was observed during the 6-month follow-up, and orthodontic treatment progressed uneventfully. This case documents the first biopsy-confirmed erosive OLP in an NF1 patient, emphasizing the importance of routine oral screening and multidisciplinary management given the potential risk of malignant transformation in OLP (approximately 1–2%).

The patient presented with a 6-month history of intermittent burning and discomfort in the buccal mucosa during orthodontic treatment. Clinical examination showed bilateral reticular white striae with erythematous erosions on the buccal mucosa, alongside classic NF1 features including multiple café-au-lait macules and neurofibromas. Differential diagnoses such as lichenoid reaction to amalgam, systemic lupus erythematosus, and drug-induced lichenoid reaction were excluded based on the absence of any amalgam restorations, negative serological tests for autoimmune markers (including ANA and anti-dsDNA), lack of systemic symptoms suggestive of SLE, and no history of medications associated with lichenoid reactions. The diagnosis of erosive OLP was clinicopathologic, supported by histopathology revealing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, basal keratinocyte necrosis, and Civatte bodies. Treatment included incisional biopsy and topical triamcinolone acetonide 0.1%, resulting in complete resolution of lesions and symptoms within one month. No recurrence was observed during the 6-month follow-up, and orthodontic treatment progressed uneventfully. This case documents the first biopsy-confirmed erosive OLP in an NF1 patient, emphasizing the importance of routine oral screening and multidisciplinary management given the potential risk of malignant transformation in OLP (approximately 1–2%).

title: Anti-Ku antibody-positive interstitial lung disease with and without established systemic autoimmune disease: a descriptive study
abstract: Abstract Background Although anti-Ku antibodies have been reported in various connective tissue diseases (CTDs), data on the clinical characteristics of anti-Ku antibody-positive interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain limited. This study investigated the clinical, radiological, and pathological features of anti-Ku antibody-positive ILD. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 13 patients with anti-Ku antibody-positive ILD at our institution between 2018 and 2025. Data on baseline characteristics, imaging, pathology, treatment, and outcomes were collected. Results Seven patients (53.8%) were diagnosed with CTDs. CTD was present in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM; n = 2), systemic sclerosis (SSc), IIM with SSc overlap, microscopic polyangiitis, rheumatoid arthritis, and Sjögren’s syndrome (n = 1, each). ILD preceded the diagnosis of CTDs in two of these patients. Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) was the most frequent pattern (n = 5, 38.5%) on chest computed tomography, followed by usual interstitial pneumonia (probable UIP, n = 4, 30.8%). On lung histopathology, the patterns were heterogeneous; fibrotic NSIP and NSIP with organizing pneumonia were each observed in two patients, whereas UIP features were present in four patients. During the observation period (mean 51.7 ± 32.1 months), four patients developed progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). Among the seven patients in whom any radiological and/or pathological UIP feature was present, four (57.1%) developed PPF or experienced acute exacerbation. Conclusions Anti-Ku antibody-positive ILD shows a heterogeneous clinical spectrum that includes both CTD-associated and non-CTD phenotypes. Progressive fibrotic disease was observed in both groups, while radiological and/or pathological UIP features may help identify patients at increased risk of disease progression.

title: Spatial artificial intelligence in gastric endoscopy for premalignant lesions and early gastric cancer: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence in gastric endoscopy increasingly produces spatial outputs to localize abnormal mucosa and define lesion extent, yet their clinical validity is uncertain. We conducted a task-specific systematic review nested within a prospectively registered parent review and identified 39 study families evaluating localization, segmentation, boundary identification, or margin delineation in gastric premalignant lesions and early gastric cancer. Most studies assessed segmentation on stored images. Histopathology often confirmed diagnosis, but spatial references were usually expert-defined endoscopic masks rather than pathology-registered boundaries. Only three studies reported patient-disjoint internal testing, six external validation, six a prospective component, and two live spatial evaluations; one study showed procedure-altering biopsy guidance. Dice, IoU, boundary, and margin measures were heterogeneous and were not pooled. Spatial AI has moved toward clinically relevant mapping and margin assessment, but stronger reference standards and validation during endoscopy are needed before these outputs can support procedural decisions.

title: Neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio and late gadolinium enhancement in clinically suspected myocarditis: a multicentre retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging identifies myocardial involvement in myocarditis and carries prognostic weight. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) combines neutrophil predominance with serum albumin, a negative acute-phase reactant. Whether NPAR is associated with LGE, and whether it adds information to its individual components and to routinely available clinical data, is unknown. Methods This retrospective observational study included 1,055 adults with clinically suspected myocarditis who underwent CMR at seven tertiary cardiovascular centres in Türkiye between October 2022 and September 2025. All studies were reviewed centrally by three cardiovascular radiologists blinded to clinical and laboratory data (Fleiss' κ = 0.83). Variables significant on univariable analysis (p < 0.10) were entered into multivariable logistic regression models, the shape of the association was examined using restricted cubic splines, and the incremental value of NPAR over the clinical and laboratory model was assessed using discrimination and reclassification metrics. Results LGE was present in 285 patients (27.0%). NPAR was higher in the LGE-positive group [1.65 (1.40–1.92) vs. 1.29 (1.02–1.55); p < 0.001]. In the multivariable model, NPAR remained independently associated with LGE positivity (adjusted odds ratio per 1 standard deviation 4.381, 95% confidence interval 3.248–5.907; p < 0.001), and the Nagelkerke R² rose from 0.157 to 0.387. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive association across the observed range with evidence of non-linearity (p = 0.013). Adding NPAR increased the area under the curve of the model from 0.728 (0.687–0.768) to 0.839 (0.806–0.872) (difference 0.111; p < 0.001), with an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (0.133–0.251) and a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.843 (0.674–1.011), both p < 0.001. As a single marker, NPAR yielded an area under the curve of 0.750 (0.718–0.782) at a cut-off of 1.43, discriminating LGE better than either constituent (both p < 0.0001). Conclusions In clinically suspected myocarditis, NPAR was independently associated with CMR-defined LGE positivity, discriminated LGE better than either of its own components, and provided significant incremental discrimination and reclassification over a clinical and laboratory model. NPAR may serve as a low-cost adjunctive marker where access to CMR is constrained.

title: Early- Versus Late-Onset Fetal Growth Restriction: Clinical Features, Placental Histopathology, and Risk Factor Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a critical adverse pregnancy complication that significantly contributes to adverse perinatal prognosis, and its clinical manifestations, pathological mechanisms and prognostic impacts vary greatly according to the gestational age of onset. Early-onset and late-onset FGR differ substantially in disease severity and underlying etiologies, to date, few studies have systematically compared the clinical characteristics and placental histopathological lesions of early- and late-onset FGR. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the clinical profiles and placental pathological changes between the two FGR subtypes and further screen key risk factors for early-onset FGR, so as to provide pathological and clinical evidence for the early identification and stratified clinical management of early-onset FGR. Methods Our cohort investigation encompassed 461 singleton pregnancies, including FGR, stratified by gestational age at diagnosis into early- and late-onset groups. Maternal demographics, pregnancy complications, delivery outcomes, Doppler parameters, and placental pathology were contrasted across groups. Multivariate regression characterized risk factors for early-onset FGR was constructed. Results Early-onset FGR was associated with significantly lower birth weight, higher preterm birth (PB) rates, worse perinatal outcomes, and more severe maternal vascular malperfusion (MVM) in placental lesions compared to late-onset FGR ( p < 0.05). Relevant risk factors associated with early-onset FGR included autoimmune disease, thyroid disorder, intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), and abnormal umbilical artery Doppler, with a particularly strong association with preeclampsia. Conclusion Early-onset FGR is characterized by greater disease severity and is strongly linked to maternal systemic conditions, placental vascular insufficiency, and aberrant Doppler hemodynamics. Early-onset FGR is fundamentally a placenta-mediated vascular disorder, compounded by secondary inflammatory activation and maternal systemic dysfunction. Targeted management of these risk factors may improve perinatal outcomes.

title: An Automated, Contamination-Controlled VQA Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language Models on 3D Oncology Imaging
abstract: Abstract Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly applied to medical imaging, yet public benchmarks may reward memorization over perception: their images and questions can enter pretraining corpora, and many items remain answerable from question text alone. We present an automated, agent-driven pipeline that builds multiple-choice benchmarks directly from paired private radiology reports and three-dimensional oncology imaging. It generates two complementary question types: schema-driven items populated deterministically from established reporting frameworks, and report-derived items verified against the source text. Because the source reports are private and single-institution, the resulting questions cannot have entered any model’s pretraining data, controlling instance-level contamination by construction. We applied the pipeline to four oncology cohorts (liver CT, liver MRI, lung CT and brain MRI; 2,509 cases and 33,870 questions) and evaluated five contemporary VLMs zero-shot. Accuracies ranged from 0.28 to 0.81 and no model was reliable across cohorts. Replacing the image with a blank input changed accuracy little for the highest-scoring models, and on schema-driven brain questions frontier models scored 0.17–0.19 higher on public than on matched private imaging. The benchmark thus separates image-dependent performance from question-text and dataset-familiarity effects, and the released pipeline lets institutions regenerate it on their own reports and images.

title: Non-contrast CT Radiomics Combined with Clinical Features for Predicting Secondary Sepsis in Severe Acute Pancreatitis
abstract: Abstract Objective: To evaluate models based on non-contrast computed tomography (CT) radiomics and early clinical data for predicting secondary sepsis in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP). Methods: This retrospective single-centre study included 253 patients with SAP admitted to the Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University between January 2021 and December 2025. Patients were allocated to a training cohort (n = 202) and an internal test cohort (n = 51) using an approximately 8:2 stratified random split. The first eligible non-contrast abdominal CT examination performed within 1 week of symptom onset was used to delineate the pancreas and contiguous peripancreatic inflammatory lesions. A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics. All candidate predictors were obtained before a prespecified prediction time point. Feature standardisation, selection and model development were conducted exclusively in the training cohort, and the training-derived classification thresholds were applied unchanged to the test cohort. Logistic regression was used to develop a clinical signature, a radiomics signature and a combined nomogram. Discrimination, calibration and clinical utility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and decision curve analysis. Results: Secondary sepsis occurred in 54 patients in the training cohort and 14 in the test cohort. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression retained eight radiomics features. In the training cohort, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.858 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.806-0.909) for the clinical signature, 0.675 (95% CI, 0.587-0.762) for the radiomics signature and 0.867 (95% CI, 0.814-0.919) for the combined nomogram. In the test cohort, the corresponding AUCs were 0.699 (95% CI, 0.542-0.855), 0.697 (95% CI, 0.550-0.843) and 0.732 (95% CI, 0.593-0.870), respectively. The combined nomogram achieved a sensitivity of 0.929 and a negative predictive value of 0.955, whereas the clinical signature achieved a specificity of 0.757. The radiomics signature showed no evidence of lack of fit in either cohort (P = 0.508 and P = 0.306). Conclusions: A radiomics signature derived from non-contrast CT may provide complementary information for risk stratification of secondary sepsis in SAP. The combined nomogram showed the highest AUC and a high negative predictive value in the internal test cohort, but its performance and calibration require confirmation and recalibration in larger external multicentre cohorts.

title: Clinical Observation of CD7-Directed CAR-T cell Therapy in Relapsed/Refractory Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukaemia
abstract: Abstract Mixed phenotype acute leukaemia (MPAL) currently lacks a specific target for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and effective treatment options for patients with relapsed/refractory disease remain limited. CD7-directed CAR-T cell therapy has achieved high complete remission rates with a favourable safety profile in patients with relapsed/refractory T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (R/R T-ALL). Given that CD7 is expressed on leukaemic blasts in a subset of patients with MPAL, we therefore used humanised CD7-directed CAR-T (hCD7 CAR-T) cells as salvage therapy in selected patients with relapsed/refractory MPAL (R/R MPAL) and evaluated the safety and efficacy of this approach. Between April 2024 to December 2025, seven patients with R/R MPAL who received hCD7 CAR-T therapy were retrospectively analysed. All patients had CD7 expression > 80% on leukaemic cells by flow cytometry. CAR-T cells were generated through transduction with a second-generation CAR lentiviral vector encoding CD3ζ-4-1BB. Before CAR-T infusion, patients received a lymphodepletion regimen based on fludarabine and/or cyclophosphamide. CAR-T cells were cultured for 5–8 days and then infused into patients. Treatment efficacy was assessed on day 30 after infusion. Minimal residual disease (MRD) was evaluated using FCM and quantitative PCR methods. Extramedullary lesions were assessed by PET/CT, CT, or ultrasonography. Patients were followed regularly until 30 April 2026. The median age was 33 years (range 18–70). Five patients had bone marrow haematological relapse (including 3 patients with extramedullary lesions), 2 patients had bone marrow MRD-positive disease, and 1 patient had relapsed after transplantation. The median infused CAR-T cell dose was 5.0 × 10⁵/kg (range 1.0–9.0 × 10⁵/kg). The major treatment-related adverse event was cytokine release syndrome (CRS), and all cases were Grade 1. Five patients received supportive treatment, 1 patient received supportive treatment and corticosteroids, and 1 patient received supportive treatment, corticosteroids, siltuximab, and etoposide. Symptoms improved in all patients, and no treatment-related mortality occurred. At day 30 after CAR-T infusion, 6 patients achieved complete remission (CR), including 1 patient with MRD-positive CR, resulting in a complete remission rate of 85.7%. One patient showed no response. The median follow-up duration was 8.3 months (range 4.7–24.4). All patients underwent bridging allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) 5–8 weeks after CAR-T therapy. Five patients achieved continuous complete remission (CCR), with remission durations of 24.4, 12.5, 6.0, 5.2, and 4.7 months, respectively. One patient relapsed at 7 months post-transplant, and one non-responder patient experienced bone marrow haematological relapse and multiple extramedullary relapses at 6.9 months post-transplant and died of disease progression. In conclusion, hCD7 CAR-T therapy demonstrated a high CR rate of 85.7% and a favourable safety profile in patients with CD7-positive R/R MPAL. Durable remissions were achievable with bridging allo-HSCT, though patients failing to respond had a poor prognosis.

title: Comparative detection performance of different imaging modalities in suspected cardiac sarcoidosis: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Background The optimal imaging modality for detecting cardiac sarcoidosis remains uncertain, since direct comparative data are largely limited to single tracer pairs. The aim of the present study was to estimate and rank the diagnostic detection performance of positron emission tomography (PET), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and conventional scintigraphy modalities in suspected cardiac sarcoidosis through a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA). Methods PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to June 2026 for studies directly comparing at least two imaging modalities. A frequentist random-effect NMA was conducted with detection rate (DR) as primary outcome, 18 F-FDG PET/CT as reference, and effect sizes expressed as risk differences (RDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Node-splitting and sensitivity analyses were applied to assess consistency and rank stability. Results Ten studies (n = 430 patients or lesions) met inclusion criteria, forming a network of nine modalities. CMR with late gadolinium enhancement (CMR-LGE) yielded the highest DR (RD 0.18 versus 18 F-FDG PET/CT; 95% CI, 0.11 to 0.25), followed by 68 Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT (RD 0.11; 95% CI, − 0.09 to 0.30); 18 F-FLT PET/CT was essentially equivalent to the reference (RD 0.00; 95% CI, − 0.23 to 0.24). 67 Ga scintigraphy yielded the lowest DR (RD − 0.73; 95% CI, − 0.82 to − 0.65). Four modalities differed significantly from 18 F-FDG PET/CT (CMR-LGE above the reference, and 67 Ga scintigraphy, 99m Tc-MIBI SPECT, and T2w-CMR below). Conclusion Our findings suggest that CMR-LGE and 68 Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT may yield a higher DR than 18 F-FDG PET/CT, while conventional radionuclide techniques appear comparatively limited. title: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis Presenting as Refractory Bilateral Lower Extremity Edema: Rapid Resolution After Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Surgery—A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Purpose Bilateral lower extremity edema is a common clinical symptom, often caused by cardiac, hepatic, renal, or venous disorders. However, the etiology of some refractory cases remains occult, and in such instances, lumbar spinal stenosis—a spinal etiology—is easily overlooked. Prolonged lower extremity edema secondary to lumbar spinal stenosis has rarely been reported in the literature, and the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms remain elusive.This case presents a unique instance where severe L4/5 lumbar spinal stenosis manifested solely as a five-year history of refractory bilateral calf edema, occurring in the complete absence of low back pain, sciatica, or neurogenic claudication. Notably, the edema resolved rapidly and completely following unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) decompression, providing direct in vivo evidence that stenosis-related edema is reversible after neural decompression. By documenting this rare presentation and its dramatic treatment response, this report aims to (1) raise awareness of a treatable spinal etiology in cryptogenic bilateral edema, (2) advocate for lumbar MRI as a screening modality, even in patients lacking overt spinal symptoms, and (3) provide mechanistic insights regarding epidural venous plexus compression and neurogenic inflammation, thereby expanding the etiological spectrum of lower extremity edema. Case Presentation A 76-year-old female presented with a five-year history of persistent symmetrical pitting edema of both calves, in the absence of low back pain, radicular pain, or motor deficits. Routine medical workup was unremarkable, with cardiac, hepatic, renal, and vascular etiologies excluded. Multiple therapeutic trials involving volume depletion strategies and diuretics proved ineffective. Subsequently, lumbar MRI and CT demonstrated severe lumbar spinal stenosis at the L4/L5 level. Results Following L4/5 unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) decompressive surgery (partial laminectomy with ligamentum flavum resection and central/lateral recess decompression under general anesthesia),bilateral calf edema markedly subsided on the first postoperative day and completely resolved by postoperative day 9.A repeat lower extremity ultrasound showed resolution of subcutaneous soft tissue edema in both calves.At the 4-week follow-up,no recurrence of lower extremity edema was observed. Conclusion This case illustrates that lumbar spinal stenosis represents a rare but reversible cause of refractory lower extremity edema. Proposed mechanisms may involve impaired venous return due to compression of the epidural venous plexus and potentially neurogenic inflammation. Lumbar MRI should be considered a screening tool for unexplained, refractory lower extremity edema. The UBE technique, as a minimally invasive and precise decompression approach, provides an effective treatment option for such patients and broadens the clinical understanding of the etiological spectrum of lower extremity edema.

title: Ultrasound-based deep learning-derived radiomics for preoperative prediction of sentinel lymph node metastasis in invasive breast cancer: a two-center retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Preoperative assessment of sentinel lymph node (SLN) metastasis may support individualized axillary management in patients with invasive breast cancer (IBC). We developed and externally validated a deep learning-derived ultrasound radiomics model for predicting SLN metastasis. Methods This retrospective two-center study included 246 patients with pathologically confirmed IBC. Center A provided 194 patients (93 with SLN metastasis), who were divided into training (n = 155) and internal test (n = 39) cohorts; 52 patients from Center B (20 with SLN metastasis) constituted an external validation cohort. Deep features were extracted from preoperative ultrasound images using a ResNet50 architecture. Feature selection was performed in the training cohort, and a gradient boosting decision tree classifier was developed. Discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis; decision curve analysis was performed as an exploratory assessment of net benefit. Results Twenty-two deep learning-derived features were retained for model development. The model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.734 (95% CI, 0.655–0.813) in the training cohort, 0.761 (95% CI, 0.601–0.920) in the internal test cohort, and 0.742 (95% CI, 0.598–0.886) in the external validation cohort. In the external cohort, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 0.769, 0.650, 0.844, 0.722, and 0.794, respectively. Decision curves are reported as exploratory analyses and do not establish clinical utility. Conclusion A deep learning-derived ultrasound radiomics model showed moderate and relatively consistent discrimination for SLN metastasis across the development and external validation cohorts. These findings support further evaluation of the model as an adjunctive preoperative risk-stratification tool; prospective validation in larger and more diverse populations is required before clinical implementation.

title: Functional Transopercular Transinsular Mesialtemporal Surgical Corridor in Mesial Temporal-Insular Tumors
abstract: Abstract Background Transcortical approaches to insula tumours have gained popularity in the recent years alongside with the widespread use of awake surgical techniques and intraoperative neuromonitoring developments. The transopercular transinsular mesialtemporal surgical corridor offers a functional approach for accessing mesial temporal-insular lesions. Case presentations and Surgical technique: A 36-year-old woman who presented with epileptic seizures and was found to have a left temporo-insular lesion on MRI. The technique performed through the temporal opercula after cortical mapping for the relevant cognitive functions – language, cognition and motor. Preoperative cortical mapping with navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation and/or functional MRI provide significant preoperative information to inform intraoperative cortical mapping. After skeletonizing the M3 branches, the approach follows a surgical structural corridor between arcuate fasciculus, superior longitudinal fasciculus system, fronto-aslant tract, and corticospinal tract superiorly and medially, inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus medially, uncinate fasciculus anteriorly, inferior and medial longitudinal fasciculus laterally and optic radiations posteriorly, reaching the mesial temporal region – uncus and hippocampal formation. At subcortical level, the boundaries of this structural corridor are functionally identified with the appropriate intraoperative testing. Asleep intraoperative testing focuses on motor evoked potentials (MEPs) mapping and monitoring using either high frequency (HFS) or low frequency (LFS) techniques, somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs) and/or cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEP). Awake intraoperative mapping and monitoring relies on the above mentioned techniques and temporary cognitive function disruption using language, social and motor cognition tasks - with either HFS or LFS techniques. Conclusion The functional transopercular transinsular mesialtemporal surgical corridor enables maximal safe resection of tumors extending to the uncus and hippocampal formation while preserving functional cortical-subcortical structures and minimizing vascular morbidity.

title: Rare bone metastasis from primary hepatic angiosarcoma: A case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Primary hepatic angiosarcoma (PHA) is a rare, aggressive vascular endothelial soft-tissue sarcoma comprising < 2% of all soft-tissue sarcomas. Unlike cutaneous or breast angiosarcoma, PHA is significantly rarer and associated with a dismal prognosis (median survival, ~ 6 months). While Kasabach-Merritt syndrome (KMS) is the most frequent hematologic complication, bone metastasis is exceedingly rare. Case presentation We report a 67-year-old man admitted with fatigue for two months and newly discovered thrombocytopenia. Comprehensive imaging and biopsy confirmed hepatic angiosarcoma with bone metastasis. Following contraindication exclusion, he received combination chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and targeted therapy. Interval abdominal CT showed stable disease without obvious tumor enlargement, though refractory thrombocytopenia persisted throughout the treatment course. Conclusion PHA typically presents with nonspecific, insidious symptoms overlapping with chronic liver disease, often resulting in delayed diagnosis. While bone marrow metastasis is rare, early bone marrow aspiration should be considered in patients with thrombocytopenia as the presenting feature. Currently, no definitive treatment regimen exists; management should be individualized and dynamically adjusted.

title: Vosoritide Treatment Does Not Change the Robust Bone Phenotype of Children with Achondroplasia
abstract: Abstract Background Vosoritide is an FDA-approved bone-lengthening treatment for children with achondroplasia, the most common form of disproportionate short stature. Whether this bone-lengthening treatment provides commensurate changes in cross-sectional morphology, to ensure bone strength is not deleteriously affected, is unknown. Thus, we sought to characterize the bone morphological parameters of children with achondroplasia on vosoritide using measurements of the second metacarpal. Methods This study included deidentified anteroposterior hand/wrist radiographs from 30 children with achondroplasia (13 males, 17 females; age 5.8 − 11.1 years). Proprietary hand films were collected at screening (pre-treatment) and at 5 years on treatment. Measurements included second metacarpal length and midshaft width, cortical thickness, robustness (total area/length) and cortical area, which correlates with strength. Measurements were compared between the two time-points via non-parametric Wilcoxon tests, and with 378 radiographs from 114 average-statured controls who did not receive vosoritide treatment (61 males, 53 females; age 6 − 16 years) via Kruskal-Wallis tests (p < 0.05). Results Compared to average-stature controls, children with achondroplasia exhibited a more robust bone phenotype (p < 0.001). After 5 years of vosoritide treatment, children with achondroplasia demonstrated increased metacarpal length and cortical area compared to their own baseline values (all p < 0.05). No sex differences were observed. Conclusions Altogether, increases in metacarpal total area and cortical area kept up with increases in metacarpal length over the course of 5 years of vosoritide treatment. As the bones lengthened, subperiosteal expansion continued at a pace which maintained robustness, allowing the bone to remain strong. This preliminary data suggests that vosoritide did not alter the naturally robust bone phenotype of children with achondroplasia. Clinical trial registration Clinical trial registry: ClinicalTrials.gov. Clinical trial numbers: NCT02055157 (registered January 13, 2014) and NCT02724228 (registered January 26, 2016).

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Shoulder Pseudodislocation Secondary to Calcific Tendinopathy: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Shoulder pseudodislocation is a rare clinical condition. Imaging examination shows displacement of the humeral head relative to the glenoid, while the osseous anatomical alignment of the joint remains intact. This article reports a 52-year-old female patient with a long history of rotator cuff calcific tendinopathy. The patient presented with recurrent chronic dull shoulder pain, recently aggravated pain, and restricted shoulder movement. Shoulder radiography revealed a dislocation-like appearance of the glenohumeral joint, calcified lesions located at the superolateral humeral head, and widening of the glenohumeral joint space. Given the absence of shoulder trauma, immediate manual reduction was not performed. Further multimodal imaging examinations including CT and MRI were completed, and the patient was finally diagnosed with shoulder pseudodislocation secondary to calcific tendinitis. CT demonstrated calcified deposits at the superolateral humeral head, whereas MRI showed supraspinatus tendon injury, extensive periarticular soft tissue edema, and glenohumeral joint capsular effusion. The patient underwent arthroscopic calcified lesion debridement combined with subacromial decompression. Postoperative radiographic reexamination at day 1 and 2 weeks revealed significant reduction of calcified lesions and gradual recovery of the abnormally widened glenohumeral joint space. Postoperative follow-up showed nearly complete relief of shoulder pain, full recovery of shoulder forward flexion, external rotation and abduction, and unremarkable limitation in daily activities. Based on this rare case, the present study aims to summarize the imaging characteristics and diagnostic and therapeutic strategies of shoulder pseudodislocation secondary to calcific tendinitis, to distinguish soft tissue-induced pseudodislocation from traumatic true shoulder dislocation, and to avoid unnecessary closed reduction. This study provides clinical evidence for preoperative imaging evaluation and minimally invasive surgical treatment of similar rare secondary shoulder lesions.

title: Fractal Geometry–Driven Hybrid Framework for Automated Skin Lesion Analysis and Classification
abstract: Abstract Skin cancer is one of the leading issues of the public health on the global level, and the ability to diagnose the presence of the malignant lesions, especially melanoma, at the initial stages is the essential factor which influences the survival rates. Recent developments in computational dermatology illustrate the necessity of interpretable, mathematically-based, and data-efficient diagnostic models. Fractal geometry presents an effective paradigm of describing the intrinsic irregularity, complexity and similarity of skin lesions particularly malignant lesions. The present paper suggests a hybrid model to incorporate fractal-based measures (boundary fractal dimension, surface fractal dimension based on Higuchi method, lacunarity, and multifractal spectra) with traditional elements of the texture (including classical features and deep visual representations, namely CNN and Vision Transformer features). The pipeline suggested comprises of preprocessing, lesion segmentation, multiscale feature extraction, feature fusion and supervised classification. Experiments based on benchmark datasets including ISIC, HAM10000, and PH2 prove that fractal features contribute greatly to the process of distinguishing benevolent and malignant lesions, and in conjunction with deep features. The findings confirm the clinical applicability, interpretation, and computational efficiency of fractal informed hybrid systems to analyze skin lesions [1–5].

title: Scalability of the Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI) in Triple- Negative Breast Cancer: A Microgravity-Induced Platform for In Silico Target Discovery
abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer remains one of modern oncology’s most critical challenges, characterized by the absence of hormone receptors and HER2 overexpression—a profile that drastically restricts targeted therapeutic options and is associated with high aggressiveness, increased metastatic risk, and unfavorable prognosis. Despite advances in genomics-based precision oncology, limitations persist regarding approaches that consider only static molecular profiles without accounting for the fundamental physical and mechanical properties of tumor cells. Here, we propose the Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI), a scalable computational platform conceived on mechanobiological principles to investigate the hypothesis that simulated microgravity conditions induce profound structural alterations in the cytoskeleton and cell adhesion complexes—a disorganization capable of exposing neoantigens and cryptic epitopes normally masked under terrestrial gravity. The methodological strategy integrates experimental models of gravitational simulation with advanced deep learning architectures: U-Net networks for segmentation and structural analysis, and Vision Transformers (ViT) to capture complex patterns of morphological deformation. The MVI calculation formula is theoretically established as a quantitative metric that synthesizes deformation magnitude, degree of structural disorganization, alterations in mechanical signaling pathways, and the level of exposure of biological targets. It is anticipated that this methodological framework, when implemented and validated in subsequent stages, will exhibit a high degree of transferability to different tumor types, constituting an innovative complementary tool for the discovery of novel therapeutic targets and for deepening the understanding of the relationships between the physical properties of tumor cells and their response to treatments.

title: Age at onset of hip osteoarthritis and joint survival in developmental dysplasia of the hip: a 20-year longitudinal study stratified by lateral center-edge angle
abstract: Abstract Background Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is a major cause of hip osteoarthritis (OA). However, few studies have evaluated OA onset age and joint preservation in relation to DDH severity. Here, we stratified DDH cases by lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) and analyzed age at radiographic OA onset and 20-year joint survival rates according to LCEA magnitude. Methods DDH cases were classified into six groups by LCEA: A, ≤ 5°; B, > 5° to ≤ 10°; C, > 10° to ≤ 15°; D, > 15° to ≤ 20°; E, > 20° to ≤ 25°; and F, > 25°. Age at OA onset was compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test. The endpoint was radiographic OA onset, and joint survival rates were calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Results In total, 151 hips were followed for a mean of 24.8 years. The distribution was 15, 17, 48, 35, 25, and 11 hips in groups A to F, respectively. Age at OA onset was in the 50s to 60s in all groups, with no significant differences (p = 0.577). The 20-year joint survival rates were 40.0%, 77.8%, 71.6%, 81.4%, 79.2%, and 90.9%, respectively, with no significant difference (p = 0.138). title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Low Bone Mass Among 937 Nursing Staff at a Tertiary Hospital in China: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background Nursing staff face multiple occupational risk factors for bone health deterioration, yet large-scale epidemiological data on bone mineral density (BMD) in this population remain limited. This study, embedded within an ongoing occupational health cohort of nurses established in 2021, aimed to investigate the prevalence of low bone mass and identify its independent risk factors among nursing staff. Methods A cross-sectional BMD sub-study was conducted in 2026 among 937 nursing staff at The First Hospital of Jilin University, China, as a follow-up wave of a nurses’ occupational health cohort initially enrolled in 2021 (n = 4,293). Forearm bone mineral density was assessed using quantitative ultrasound (BMD-A3, Pinyuan Medical, Jiangsu, China). Low bone mass was defined as a T-score < − 1.0. Data on demographics, lifestyle, reproductive factors, occupational factors, and nutritional habits were collected via questionnaire. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors. A prediction model was internally validated using ROC curve, calibration plot, and decision curve analysis. Results The prevalence of low bone mass was 21.7% (203/937), including 20.6% with osteopenia and 1.1% with osteoporosis. Multivariate logistic regression identified four independent factors: menopause (OR = 4.06, 95% CI 2.12–7.76, P < 0.001), history of falls (OR = 1.69, 95% CI 1.10–2.59, P = 0.016), sedentary behavior (OR = 1.53, 95% CI 1.10–2.13, P = 0.011), and history of fractures (OR = 0.33, 95% CI 0.13–0.86, P = 0.023). The model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.661 (95% CI 0.628–0.710), with good calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow χ² = 4.81, P = 0.778) and net clinical benefit at threshold probabilities between 10% and 35%. Subgroup analyses confirmed the consistency of menopause across strata and showed amplified effects of sedentary behavior in overweight/obese individuals. Conclusions Menopause was the strongest risk factor for low bone mass, while sedentary behavior and falls were independent modifiable risk factors. Achieving recommended exercise levels did not fully offset the detrimental effects of prolonged sedentary behavior. These findings support workplace interventions targeting sedentary behavior reduction and BMD screening for peri-menopausal nursing staff.

title: Endometriosis/Adenomyosis and Congenital Uterine Malformations: Correlation of ESHRE/ESGE classes to #ENZIAN compartments
abstract: Abstract Purpose Identify the association between endometriosis/adenomyosis and Congenital Uterine Malformations (CUMs), determine the malformation most commonly associated and detect the #Enzian compartment most frequently involved. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 304 patients with CUMs diagnosed by three-dimensional transvaginal ultrasound (3D-TVS) according to the ESHRE/ESGE classification, referred to our Gynecological Ultrasound Unit between January 2022 and December 2025. Concurrent endometriosis/adenomyosis was assessed by 2D/3D-TVS, and lesion distribution was analyzed according to the #Enzian classification. Results Among the 304 patients, 44 (14.5%) had dysmorphic uterus (ESHRE U1), 193 (63.5%) septate uterus (U2), 30 (9.8%) bicorporeal uterus (U3), 35 (11.5%) hemi-uterus (U4), and 2 (0.6%) aplastic uterus (U5). Overall, 116 patients (38.2%) showed at least one ultrasound sign of endometriosis/adenomyosis: 22/44 (50%) U1, 80/193 (41.5%) U2, 5/30 (16.7%) U3, 9/35 (25.7%) U4, and none with U5. U3 showed the lowest association with endometriosis/adenomyosis (OR 0.29). Multivariate logistic regression identified significant associations for U1 (OR 5.0) and U2 (OR 3.5). Analysis of the #Enzian compartments showed that U1 was associated with the FA compartment (OR 8.00), whereas U2 was associated with DIE compartment (A + B+C + FB; OR 5.16). No significant association was found for U3, U4, or U5. Conclusion CUMs are associated with endometriosis/adenomyosis and may influence lesion distribution. U2 is mainly associated with DIE, whereas U1 is primarily associated with the FA compartment. These findings support the integration of advanced 3D-TVS and the #Enzian classification in the assessment of patients with CUMs. Preoperative identification of anomaly-specific endometriotic patterns may improve diagnostic accuracy and guide minimally invasive surgical planning.

title: Association between preoperative proximal humeral Hounsfield unit values and structural healing after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background: Local bone quality may influence suture-anchor fixation and tendon-to-bone healing after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR). Hounsfield unit (HU) values derived from computed tomography (CT) may provide a quantitative surrogate measure of regional cancellous bone quality. We investigated the association between preoperative proximal humeral HU values and 12-month structural healing after ARCR and assessed the discriminative performance of HU values for unfavorable structural healing. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 126 patients with full-thickness supraspinatus tears who underwent primary arthroscopic suture-bridge repair between January 2020 and December 2024 and had both preoperative shoulder CT and 12-month postoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Proximal humeral HU values were calculated as the mean of measurements obtained at three equidistant axial cancellous-bone levels between the humeral head apex and the surgical neck. Structural integrity was assessed using the Sugaya classification. Sugaya types I–II were categorized as favorable healing and types III–V as unfavorable healing. Group comparisons, Spearman rank correlation, multivariable logistic regression with HU modeled per 10-unit increase, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed. Results: Of the 126 patients, 78 had favorable structural healing and 48 had unfavorable structural healing. Mean proximal humeral HU values were lower in the unfavorable-healing group than in the favorable-healing group (63.67 ± 31.82 vs 90.54 ± 38.43, P < 0.001). HU values were moderately inversely correlated with Sugaya grade (Spearman ρ = −0.425, P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, tear size, Goutallier grade, and supraspinatus muscle occupation ratio (SGOR), each 10-HU increase was associated with lower odds of unfavorable structural healing (adjusted OR, 0.822; 95% CI, 0.682–0.990; P = 0.039). Larger tear size was independently associated with higher odds of unfavorable healing, whereas higher SGOR was associated with lower odds. The AUC for HU values was 0.784. An exploratory cutoff of 87.5 HU yielded a sensitivity of 85.1% and a specificity of 51.3%. Conclusions: Lower preoperative proximal humeral HU values were independently associated with unfavorable structural healing at 12 months after ARCR. Opportunistic HU assessment may provide complementary information on local bone-related risk; however, its modest specificity suggests that HU values should be interpreted alongside tear size and muscle-quality measures rather than as a standalone diagnostic threshold.

title: The First Case Report of Human Leukocyte Antigen Typing in a Taiwanese Patient with Diffuse Panbronchiolitis
abstract: Abstract Backgrounds: Diffuse panbronchiolitis (DPB) is an idiopathic inflammatory disease characterized by inflammation of the respiratory bronchioles. Typical symptoms include exertional dyspnea, persistent productive cough, and sputum production. Progressive airflow limitation can occur in individuals with pre-existing respiratory diseases. Case presentation: A 32-year-old male Taiwanese patient with history of chronic sinusitis and asthma visited our hospital with acute-onset breathlessness, productive cough, and postnasal drip. Lung auscultation revealed crackles and wheezes. High-resolution computed tomography showed diffuse centrilobular micronodules in both lungs, while pulmonary function tests indicated moderate mixed airflow restriction and obstruction. His human leukocyte antigen (HLA) typing revealed the presence of B54/B55 susceptible alleles. With the fulfillment of diagnostic criteria for DPB, a combination therapy approach of low-dose erythromycin and corticosteroids was initiated, leading to significant improvement in symptoms, radiographic lesions, and lung dysfunction. Conclusions This is the first report of a Taiwanese patient with DPB to have HLA-B54/B55 susceptible gene. The final piece of HLA typing puzzle in East Asian populations is completed. This case underscores the importance of early diagnosis and effective management of concurrent DPB and asthma, demonstrating that prompt therapeutic intervention can yield favorable outcomes.

title: IL-17+ lymphocytes mark low-immunity, EMT-enriched tumors in primary triple-negative breast cancer: investigated in relation to tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (CD8+, CD4+, FOXP3+) and macrophages (CD163+)
abstract: Abstract Background The immunological response in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is of clinical value. In this study, we investigated the prognostic relevance of distinct immune cell subpopulations in TNBC, their interrelationships and their associated molecular profiles. Material & methods IL-17+, CD8+, CD4+ and FOXP3+ lymphocytes and CD163+ macrophages were quantified by immunohistochemistry in tissue microarrays, while tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) were assessed on H&E-stained slides in a population-based Swedish cohort of 237 patients with early-stage TNBC diagnosed 2010-2015. Chemotherapy (CT) was administered to 171 patients (155 adjuvant, 16 neoadjuvant). Analyses were conducted on CT-naive tumor tissue. Survival was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression and molecular profiling performed by analysing RNA-sequencing data. Results High CD8+, CD4+, FOXP3+ and stromal CD163+ were all positively correlated and associated with improved prognosis in CT-treated patients. In contrast, IL-17+ lymphocytes were inversely correlated with TILs and the other immune cell subsets and their prognostic impact was non-significant, although hazard ratios suggested a potential adverse prognostic effect for invasive disease-free survival. RNA-sequencing analysis demonstrated that tumors infiltrated with IL-17+ lymphocytes were characterized by enrichment of epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) and pathways associated with metabolic reprogramming and cellular stress adaptation, while immune/inflammatory- and cell cycle-related pathways showed weak or no enrichment. The enrichment pattern for IL-17+ tumors contrasted with those high in TILs and the other immune cell subpopulations. Conclusions This study demonstrates that primary TNBC tumors infiltrated by IL-17+ lymphocytes represent a distinct phenotype characterized by enrichment of EMT and reduced overall immune activity, with potential implications for patient stratification and therapeutic strategies. Trial Registration The Swedish Cancerome Analysis Network – Breast (SCAN-B) study was retrospectively registered 2 nd Dec 2014 at ClinicalTrials.gov; ID NCT02306096.

title: Evaluation of CBCT-based HU correction for synthetic CT generation in head-and-neck radiotherapy: FOV-stratified and peripheral-region analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is essential for image-guided radiotherapy for head and neck (H&N) cancer but suffers from inaccurate Hounsfield units (HUs) due to scatter, artifacts, and field of view (FOV) truncation, limiting its use for dose calculation. We aimed to compare linear correction, a residual U-Net model (ResUNet), and a paired cycle-consistent conditional GAN (PCC-cGAN) framework with residual U-Net generators for HU correction and synthetic CT (sCT) generation, the deep learning models trained in a paired setting, with the CycleGAN variant adapted from its original unpaired design to exploit cycle-consistency in addition to supervised training. Our evaluation emphasizes FOV stratification (complete vs. truncated) and spatial localization of residual errors. This study provides an FOV-stratified and peripheral-aware evaluation of CBCT-based HU correction, highlighting residual error patterns that may be overlooked by global MAE analysis alone. Methods A total of 100 CBCT/CT pairs from 67 H&N patients were divided into complete FOV (19 pairs) and truncated FOV (81 pairs) groups. Evaluation was performed within three spatial mask regions: intersection, eroded intersection, and peripheral. An independent-patient sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess patient‑level overlap. Preliminary body‑level dosimetric consistency was evaluated by comparing raw CBCT and ResUNet sCT against the reference planning CT (pCT) dose using gamma pass rates (2%/2mm and 3%/3mm) and dose Mean Absolute Error & Root Mean Squared Error (MAE/RMSE). Results ResUNet achieved the lowest HU-MAE across the evaluated regions in both FOV groups. In the independent-patient subset, this pattern was preserved for intersection and eroded mask regions, with ResUNet performing best in nearly all of the patient-region combinations. The peripheral MAE remained substantially higher than the intersection and eroded MAE for all methods (e.g., ResUNet: 171.51 vs. 76.93 HU in the complete FOV). Body‑level gamma pass rates (GPR) and dose metrics were generally maintained or modestly improved by ResUNet, but HU improvements did not translate proportionally to dosimetric gains across all patients. Conclusions ResUNet provided the lowest HU-MAE among the evaluated methods under the conditions of this study for CBCT-based sCT generation in H&N radiotherapy, with persistent residual errors concentrated at the peripheral evaluation region, where the highest residual MAE was observed. The FOV-stratified and peripheral-aware evaluation framework introduced here informs future DVH-based validation and dose-of-the-day adaptive workflows.

title: From Quantification to Differentiation: T2 Mapping for Mucinous Components in Primary and Post-neoadjuvant Rectal Cancers
abstract: Abstract Objective To quantitatively assess mucin content in rectal mucinous adenocarcinoma and adenocarcinoma with mucinous components using T2 mapping, and to further evaluate its performance in distinguishing post-neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) mucinous degeneration from primary rectal mucinous adenocarcinoma, thereby providing reliable imaging evidence for individualized treatment strategies. Methods This study consisted of two interrelated phases. Phase 1 investigated the correlation between T2 values and tumor mucin content. Phase 2 evaluated the diagnostic efficacy of T2 mapping for differentiating post-nCRT mucinous degeneration from primary mucinous adenocarcinoma. Patients who underwent rectal cancer surgery at our institution between January 2021 and June 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. For Phase 1, 55 patients were enrolled and divided into three groups based on postoperative pathological mucin content: mucinous adenocarcinoma group (MAC, mucin ≥ 50%, n = 15); adenocarcinoma with mucinous component group (AMC, mucin < 50%, n = 20); and conventional adenocarcinoma group (AC, no mucin component, n = 20). For Phase 2, 27 patients were enrolled, including 12 with post-nCRT mucinous degeneration and 15 with primary mucinous adenocarcinoma. All patients underwent pelvic MRI including T2 mapping within 1–2 weeks before surgery. Two radiologists independently performed ROI delineation. For Phase 1, ROIs were drawn along the tumor margin covering all tumor parenchyma while avoiding necrosis, cystic areas, and intraluminal contents. For Phase 2, ROIs were restricted to mucinous areas (hyperintense on T2-weighted images). Mean T2 values (ms) were automatically calculated. Phase 1 used univariate and multivariate regression to assess correlation with mucin content and diagnostic performance among the three groups. Phase 2 compared T2 values between the two groups and performed ROC curve analysis. Results (1) Phase 1: T2 values showed a strong positive correlation with pathological mucin content (Rs = 0.877, P < 0.001). Significant differences in T2 values were observed among the three groups (P < 0.001). For distinguishing AC from AMC, the AUC was 0.8175, sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.70, optimal cutoff value 89.14 ms. Leave‑one‑out cross‑validation (LOOCV) confirmed the robustness of this cutoff (mean 89.58 ms, range 89.14–90.01 ms), with a cross‑validated AUC of 0.805. For distinguishing AMC from MAC, the AUC was 0.9867, sensitivity 0.93, specificity 1.00, optimal cutoff value 117.92 ms. LOOCV yielded a mean cutoff of 118.02 ms (range 117.41–121.97 ms) and a cross‑validated AUC of 0.930. (2) Phase 2: T2 values in the post-nCRT mucinous degeneration group (median, 156.34 ms) were significantly lower than those in the primary MAC group (median, 198.76 ms; P < 0.05). The AUC for differentiating the two groups was 0.825, sensitivity 0.83, specificity 0.80, optimal cutoff value 181.92 ms. LOOCV demonstrated a mean cutoff of 187.91 ms (range 187.84–187.93 ms) and a cross‑validated AUC of 0.772. Conclusion T2 mapping enables quantitative assessment of mucin content in rectal cancer, demonstrating a strong positive correlation with pathological mucin content and effective discrimination among MAC, AMC, and AC. Furthermore, T2 mapping effectively distinguishes post-nCRT mucinous degeneration from primary mucinous adenocarcinoma, providing a potential imaging tool for preoperative evaluation that may assist in treatment planning pending prospective validation.

title: Spread through air spaces in lung adenocarcinoma with subsequent contralateral metachronous pulmonary lesion: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Spread through air spaces (STAS) is a pattern of invasion in lung adenocarcinoma introduced by the World Health Organization in 2015. STAS is associated with increased recurrence risk and reduced survival. Herein, we report a case of lung adenocarcinoma with STAS in which cinematic rendering provided intuitive three-dimensional visualization of satellite nodules, followed by a contralateral pulmonary lesion 18 months later harboring a de novo EGFR T790M/L858R double mutation, managed with surgery and adjuvant almonertinib. Case presentation A 53-year-old Chinese woman had a pulmonary mass incidentally discovered on chest CT during a routine medical examination. Chest CT revealed a 2.8 cm mass in the left lower lobe with multiple peritumoral satellite nodules. Cinematic rendering reconstruction clearly depicted the satellite nodules and their spatial relationship with adjacent structures. The patient underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) left lower lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection. Postoperative pathology confirmed invasive lung adenocarcinoma (acinar predominant, with papillary [20%], micropapillary [15%], and focal poorly differentiated [5%] components) with STAS, pathological stage pT1cN0cM0 (AJCC 9th edition). No adjuvant therapy was administered. Follow-up chest CT every 6 months revealed a new 0.6 cm nodule in the right middle lobe 18 months postoperatively. The patient underwent VATS right middle lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection. Pathology confirmed a second invasive lung adenocarcinoma (acinar 40%, papillary 40%, micropapillary 20%, grade 3), stage pT1aN0cM0. Genetic testing revealed EGFR T790M (exon 20) and L858R (exon 21) double mutation. The patient was started on adjuvant almonertinib (110 mg daily) and remained recurrence-free at 20 months of almonertinib therapy. Conclusions This case demonstrates that peritumoral satellite nodules on CT reliably indicate STAS, and STAS-positive patients require vigilant surveillance for metachronous pulmonary lesions. Cinematic rendering provides intuitive visualization of STAS-related satellite nodules, aiding surgical planning. The de novo EGFR T790M/L858R double mutation in the metachronous lesion raises important considerations regarding tumor clonality, possible germline EGFR T790M, and the role of third-generation EGFR-TKIs as adjuvant therapy.

title: Diagnosing Susac Syndrome Despite Incomplete Clinical Triad: A Case Report of Convergent Atypical Neuroimaging and Inflammatory Cerebrospinal Fluid Findings: Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Susac syndrome (SuS) is a rare autoimmune endotheliopathy involving the brain, retina, and inner ear. Because patients frequently present without the complete clinical triad of encephalopathy, branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAO), and sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), diagnosis can be challenging. The European Susac Consortium (EuSaC) criteria classify SuS according to objective involvement of the brain, retinal, and vestibulocochlear domains; however, many patients do not fulfill criteria for probable or definite disease at initial presentation. Furthermore, neuroimaging and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings may overlap with inflammatory demyelinating disorders such as multiple sclerosis (MS). We report a case where EuSaC criteria was not met, however there was strong clinical and radiographic evidence to support the diagnosis of SuS. This case brings to question whether strict fulfillment of EuSaC criteria is needed to initiate early inpatient treatment to prevent irreversible neurological deficits. Case presentation We report the case of a woman in her early forties with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease, recurrent ischemic strokes, and an unspecified hypercoagulable disorder who presented with progressive gait instability, dizziness, and bilateral lower extremity weakness. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated characteristic central corpus callosum “snowball” lesions and cerebellar leptomeningeal enhancement. CSF analysis revealed elevated immunoglobulin G (IgG) index, elevated IgG synthesis rate, and markedly elevated myelin basic protein (MBP) in the absence of oligoclonal bands (OCB). At the time of presentation, only the brain domain of the EuSaC criteria was objectively fulfilled, and the patient therefore did not meet criteria for probable or definite SuS. Nevertheless, the characteristic neuroimaging phenotype, inflammatory CSF profile without oligoclonal bands, and absence of typical MS features strongly favored SuS and prompted treatment with high dose steroids and further diagnostic evaluation. Conclusions This case demonstrates that strict fulfillment of EuSaC criteria may not be required to recognize SuS when characteristic neuroradiographic findings and supportive clinical features are present. Recognition of central corpus callosum “snowball” lesions and cerebellar leptomeningeal enhancement may facilitate earlier diagnosis and treatment, potentially reducing irreversible neurologic, retinal, and auditory morbidity.

title: A Dangerous Evolution of Retroperitoneal Infection to Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Pseudoaneurysm: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the infrarenal abdominal aorta is a rare and potentially fatal complication of infection. Early diagnosis can be challenging because clinical symptoms are often nonspecific, and initial imaging may demonstrate only inflammatory changes without aneurysmal formation. This case highlights the importance of recognizing evolving radiographic findings in patients with a history of recurrent infection. Case presentation A 46-year-old man with a history of recurrent pelvic abscesses secondary to diverticulitis presented with three days of back pain, nausea, and vomiting. Initial imaging demonstrated a retroperitoneal inflammatory mass encasing the infrarenal aorta without evidence of pseudoaneurysm. Repeat imaging two weeks later demonstrated interval development of a pseudoaneurysm, raising concern for an infected aortic process. The patient underwent midline exploratory laparotomy with definitive surgical management and subsequently completed six weeks of intravenous antimicrobial therapy. He had an uncomplicated recovery with resolution of the infection and no reported recurrence. Conclusions Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the abdominal aorta should be considered in patients with systemic or localized infection and new, unexplained back or abdominal pain, particularly when inflammatory changes surround the aorta on imaging. Serial imaging may be critical for identifying rapid progression from periaortic inflammation to pseudoaneurysm formation. Early recognition and definitive surgical management combined with prolonged antimicrobial therapy can prevent rupture and improve outcomes.

title: Learning Adaptive Gated Fusion of Convolutional and Transformer Features for Generalizable Medical Image Classification
abstract: Abstract Accurate and generalizable classification of medical images remains a central challenge for computer aided diagnosis because convolutional neural networks capture fine grained local texture while vision transformers capture long range global structure, and existing hybrid designs typically combine the two with a fixed rule that cannot adjust to the varying diagnostic importance of local versus global cues across imaging domains [12, 22, 37]. This paper proposes DACANet, a dual path network in which an EfficientNet backbone and a vision transformer backbone extract complementary features that are combined through a learned adaptive gating mechanism, allowing the network to decide, per sample, how much weight to place on local convolutional evidence relative to global transformer evidence before classification. The network was evaluated on three public datasets spanning three diagnostic domains, dermoscopic skin lesion images from HAM10000, magnetic resonance images of brain tumors, and retinal fundus images for diabetic retinopathy grading from APTOS 2019, without any dataset specific tuning. DACANet achieved a best validation accuracy of 87.37 percent on HAM10000, 95.25 percent on the brain tumor dataset, and 84.64 percent on APTOS 2019. An ablation study replacing the adaptive gate with a fixed fusion rule showed adaptive gating improved accuracy on the two more visually heterogeneous datasets by 1.65 and 0.68 percentage points respectively, while performing within 0.19 percentage points of the fixed baseline on the simpler brain tumor dataset. These findings indicate that adaptive fusion is most beneficial when the relative importance of local and global cues varies across samples, offering a practical, reproducible framework for trustworthy, cross domain medical image classification, in line with Sustainable Development Goal 9 on industry, innovation and infrastructure.

title: CT-Based Radiomic Models for Stage Stratification and Relapse Prediction in Colon Cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and validate computed tomography (CT)-based radiomic models for differentiating stage II from stage III colon cancer and predicting 5-year relapse risk. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, 104 patients with colon cancer who underwent preoperative CT between December 2016 and September 2022 were included. Primary tumors were manually segmented in three dimensions, and 105 radiomic features were extracted together with preoperative clinical variables. The dataset was randomly divided into a training cohort (70%) and an independent validation cohort (30%). Model development and optimization were performed using 10-fold cross-validation within the training cohort. Separate machine learning models were developed for stage differentiation (n = 84) and 5-year relapse prediction (n = 104). Model performance was evaluated in the validation cohort using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results: For stage differentiation, the generalized linear model achieved an AUC of 0.760 in the validation cohort, with a balanced accuracy of 0.744 and a sensitivity of 0.889 for identifying stage II disease. For 5-year relapse prediction, the partial least squares model showed the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.910 and a sensitivity of 0.950. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent predictive performance in stage II (AUC, 0.929) and stage III disease (AUC, 0.926). Conclusion: CT-derived radiomic features enabled differentiation between stage II and stage III colon cancer and showed prognostic value for predicting 5-year relapse. These findings support the potential role of radiomics as a noninvasive imaging biomarker for preoperative risk stratification in colon cancer.

title: Low-grade Oncocytic Fumarate Hydratase-deficient Renal Cell Carcinoma in a Patient with Hereditary Leiomyomatosis and Renal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Fumarate hydratase (FH)-deficient renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is generally an aggressive, high-grade tumor with a poor prognosis. We report a case of low-grade oncocytic FH-deficient RCC with a favorable course and discuss it in the context of the genotype-phenotype relationship in FH-deficient RCC. Case presentation: A woman in her 70s was found to have bilateral multifocal renal tumors on PET-CT performed during the work-up of a left cervical mass. She underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy of the left kidney. Histopathology showed a low-grade oncocytic renal tumor (pT1aNXMX, WHO/ISUP grade 2) without sarcomatoid change or necrosis, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated loss of FH expression with 2SC positivity, establishing the diagnosis of low-grade oncocytic FH-deficient RCC. Germline genetic testing identified a heterozygous FH missense variant, c.584T > C (p.Met195Thr), confirming hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome. The pedigree showed maternal-line uterine leiomyomatosis consistent with autosomal dominant transmission. The postoperative course was uneventful, with no recurrence or metastasis. The cervical mass proved to be a benign thyroid nodule unrelated to the renal tumor. Conclusion FH-deficient RCC can present as a low-grade, organ-confined tumor with a favorable course. The identical germline FH variant (p.Met195Thr) has elsewhere caused an aggressive tumor, underscoring that the germline genotype does not by itself determine prognosis. Management according to FH-deficient RCC and genetic counseling of relatives remain essential.

title: CSF Diversion Facilitates Further Systemic Therapy in Leptomeningeal Hydrocephalus
abstract: Abstract Background Leptomeningeal disease (LMD) is a complication of metastatic cancer frequently accompanied by symptomatic hydrocephalus. CSF shunting has traditionally been considered palliative, providing symptomatic relief. In the era of CNS-penetrating systemic therapies, factors associated with post-shunt outcomes remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated clinical outcomes following CSF shunting for LMD-associated hydrocephalus and identified predictors of oncologic benefit. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of 51 consecutive patients with LMD-associated hydrocephalus who underwent CSF shunting. Clinical, radiographic, molecular, treatment, and outcome data were collected. The primary endpoint was symptomatic improvement and receipt of post-shunt oncologic therapy. Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox regression. Results We included 51 patients with a median pre-shunt KPS of 60. Brain metastases were present in 60.8% and breast cancer (43.1%) was the most common. Clinical improvement occurred in 40 of 49 evaluable patients (81.6%), with the greatest improvement in nausea/vomiting (62.5%) and headache (58.1%). Following shunting, 41 patients (80.4%) received additional oncologic therapy, including 20 (39.2%) who received CNS-penetrating therapy. Median OS was 70 days (95% CI, 54–156). CNS-penetrating therapy was associated with longer survival (193 vs. 49 days; log-rank p = 0.0001). In multivariable analysis, cranial nerve involvement was independently associated with worse survival (HR 4.25, 95% CI 1.75–10.32; p = 0.001), whereas post-shunt therapy (HR 0.078, 95% CI 0.022–0.282; p < 0.001) and CNS-penetrating therapy (HR 0.266, 95% CI 0.116–0.612; p = 0.002) were associated with improved survival. Brain metastases were also associated with inferior survival (HR 2.86, 95% CI 1.10–7.46; p = 0.032). Conclusions CSF shunting provides meaningful symptomatic benefit in patients with LMD-associated hydrocephalus and enables subsequent treatment. Receipt of CNS-penetrating therapy was associated with prolonged survival, whereas cranial nerve involvement and brain metastases identified patients with poorer prognosis. These findings support integrating CSF diversion with contemporary CNS-active therapies in selected patients with LMD.

title: A Tensor Greedy Double-Block Extended Kaczmarz Method for Inconsistent Tensor Linear Systems under the t-product
abstract: Abstract The randomized extended Kaczmarz method is an effective iterative framework for solving large-scale inconsistent linear systems. In this paper, we extend this framework to third-order inconsistent tensor linear systems under the t-product and propose the Tensor Greedy Double Block Extended Kaczmarz (TGDBEK) method. At each iteration, TGDBEK dynamically constructs active blocks of row and column slices via a residual-based greedy selection strategy, prioritizing the slices associated with the largest residual norms. Unlike existing tensor block Kaczmarz variants that rely on static, predefined partitions --- the tensor randomized extended block Kaczmarz (TREBK) method, its greedy counterpart (TREGBK), and the tensor randomized extended average block Kaczmarz (TREABK) method --- TGDBEK adapts the active block sizes dynamically at each step using a single intuitive threshold parameter $\eta$. We establish the theoretical linear convergence of TGDBEK to the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution $\mathcal{A}^\dagger * \mathcal{B}$. Extensive numerical benchmarks on synthetic dense and sparse tensor systems, as well as multidimensional multichannel color and 3D volumetric MRI image deblurring problems, demonstrate that TGDBEK substantially outperforms state-of-the-art tensor Kaczmarz solvers in both iteration count and CPU running time.

Extensive numerical benchmarks on synthetic dense and sparse tensor systems, as well as multidimensional multichannel color and 3D volumetric MRI image deblurring problems, demonstrate that TGDBEK substantially outperforms state-of-the-art tensor Kaczmarz solvers in both iteration count and CPU running time.
